嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄序
聖朝設科以經術取士率三載而
一舉蓋監古鄉舉里選之法
而遠過者也嘉靖歲辛酉貴
州又當大比士巡按監察御
史巫繼咸職當監臨奉
命馳至乃以前御史黃國用禮聘
===
明經博士以錄暨陳安常若
愚黃龍梁士楚充考試官比
入院則左布政使楊守約右
叅議徐敎領提調副使張廷
栢僉事蔣春生領監試凡內
外愼擇可者而後授事御史
陳事周愼肅布紀綱務精白
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄序

聖朝設科，以經術取士，率三載而一舉，蓋監古鄉舉里選之法而遠過者也。嘉靖歲辛酉，貴州又當大比士。巡按監察御史巫繼咸職當監臨，奉命馳至，乃以前御史黃國用禮聘明經博士以錄暨陳安常、若愚、黃龍、梁士楚充考試官。比入院，則左布政使楊守約、右叅議徐敎領提調，副使張廷栢、僉事蔣春生領監試。凡內外，愼擇可者而後授事。御史陳事周愼，肅布紀綱，務精白
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

Our sagely dynasty established examinations to select men through their mastery of the Classics, ordinarily holding them once every three years. This system takes as its model the ancient practice of recommending men from districts and selecting them from villages, yet far surpasses it. In the xinyou year of the Jiajing reign [1561], Guizhou was again due to hold the triennial examination of scholars. Wu Jixian, Regional Inspector and Investigating Censor, was responsible for serving as Supervising Official. He hastened there in obedience to his commission. He then had the former censor Huang Guoyong formally invite the erudite in classical learning Yilu, together with Chen Anchang, Ruoyu, Huang Long, and Liang Shichu, to serve as Examiners [the wording and division of names here are uncertain].

When they entered the examination compound, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Yang Shouyue and Right Administration Assistant Xu Jiao took charge as Proctors, while Surveillance Vice Commissioner Zhang Tingbai and Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Jiang Chunsheng directed the supervision of the examination. For all duties inside and outside the compound, suitable men were carefully selected before being assigned their tasks. The censor arranged matters thoroughly and circumspectly, solemnly promulgated rules and discipline, and strove for absolute integrity …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
爲百執事先乃合提學副使
況叔祺所選士一千有奇旣
三試得其儁三十人次其名
氏若其文之可式者以
獻綵以役事宜宣言於首簡竊
惟唐虞三代之盛治博稽載
籍可攷而知近者侯甸遠者
===
要荒莫不靡然顮化其在要
服則唯聲敎加焉固未聞其
興文物登賢良儼然與中國
齒也貴州古要服及我
文皇帝疆理天下始設藩臣部署
之
皇上中興文敎四達貴州得專貢
punctuated:
爲百執事先。乃合提學副使況叔祺所選士一千有奇，旣三試，得其儁三十人，次其名氏，若其文之可式者，以獻。綵以役事，宜宣言於首簡。
竊惟唐虞三代之盛治，博稽載籍，可攷而知。近者侯甸，遠者要荒，莫不靡然顮化。其在要服，則唯聲敎加焉，固未聞其興文物、登賢良，儼然與中國齒也。貴州古要服，及我文皇帝疆理天下，始設藩臣部署之。皇上中興，文敎四達，貴州得專貢
translation_en:
…to set an example for all the functionaries. Thereupon, the more than one thousand candidates selected by Kuang Shuqi, the Education Intendant and Vice Commissioner, were assembled. After three examination sessions, thirty outstanding men were selected. Their names were arranged in order, together with those of their compositions that could serve as models, for presentation to the throne. I, Cai, having taken part in this undertaking, ought to offer some words on its opening pages.
I humbly reflect that the flourishing governance of the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties can be known through extensive examination of the written records. From the nearby lordly and royal domains to the distant outer and wilderness zones, all yielded to their transforming influence [?]. Yet in the outer zone, only the influence of their civilizing instruction extended there; we have certainly never heard of its cultivating the refinements of civilization and advancing worthy and able men so as to stand fully on an equal footing with the Central Lands. Guizhou was anciently part of this outer zone. Only when our Emperor Wen ordered the territories of the realm were provincial officials first established to administer it. Under His Majesty’s restoration of flourishing rule, literary learning and moral instruction have reached in every direction, and Guizhou has been enabled to submit its own candidates…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
舉視諸藩同士應感而興烝
烝嚮用蓋千古之希覯六籍
之所不能談者也夫
聖作物覩悠久無疆草莽之臣比
屋可舉況我
國家疆理之域
聖天子所加志者哉 自受聘以
===
來輒沾沾自喜因念孱工管
穴無可以仰稱
明德乃今幸而在事儹附於以人
事君者之義爲庸多矣退而
深惟曰未也聖人之官人猶
匠之用木榱題棟桷務勝其
任無寧以不材錯置之其直
punctuated:
舉，視諸藩同。士應感而興，烝烝嚮用，蓋千古之希覯、六籍之所不能談者也。夫聖作物覩，悠久無疆，草莽之臣比屋可舉，況我國家疆理之域、聖天子所加志者哉！
自受聘以來，輒沾沾自喜，因念孱工管穴，無可以仰稱明德。乃今幸而在事，儹附於以人事君者之義，爲庸多矣。退而深惟曰：「未也。聖人之官人，猶匠之用木，榱題棟桷，務勝其任，無寧以不材錯置之？其直
translation_en:
…recruitment through the examinations, on the same footing as the other provinces. Its scholars have responded to this influence and risen to the occasion, advancing eagerly toward service. This is surely a sight rarely witnessed through the ages, something of which even the Six Classics could not speak. When the sage arises, all behold him; his influence endures without limit. Worthy men living outside official service can be recommended from household after household—how much more so within the territory administered by our dynasty, to which the sagely Son of Heaven has devoted his attention!
Ever since accepting the invitation to serve, I have repeatedly felt pleased with myself. Yet I reflect that my feeble abilities and narrow understanding offer nothing adequate to match the illustrious virtue above. Now, fortunately participating in this undertaking, I may associate myself [?] with the principle of serving one’s ruler by finding worthy men: this would be a considerable contribution. Withdrawing and reflecting deeply, however, I said: “Not yet. The sage’s appointment of men to office resembles a carpenter’s use of timber. Whether for projecting rafter ends, ridgepoles, or rafters, he must ensure that each is adequate to its task. How could he misplace unsuitable timber among them? Those whose straightness…”

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
中繩方圓中規矩材木也㮚
櫟之木雖大無所取材比年
有事
明堂徵材黔中諸部求之者不遺
餘力矣卽使不程其材而雜
以㮚櫟將焉用之乃今以尺
寸之枝而論士則其言勁而
===
正閎而深疏達而有直體材
矣行將得一當
聖主俾各盡其所長豈惟其材之
足多而在事者且自託於不
朽使徒言有枝葉顧昌然舉
之而終不可以納於軌物登
於
punctuated: 中繩，方圓中規矩，材木也。㮚櫟之木雖大，無所取材。比年有事明堂，徵材黔中諸部，求之者不遺餘力矣。卽使不程其材，而雜以㮚櫟，將焉用之？乃今以尺寸之枝而論士，則其言勁而正，閎而深，疏達而有直體，材矣。行將得一當聖主，俾各盡其所長，豈惟其材之足多，而在事者且自託於不朽。使徒言有枝葉，顧昌然舉之，而終不可以納於軌物，登於
translation_en: …conform to the carpenter’s inked line, and in their square and round forms conform to the square and compass: these are usable timbers. Chestnut and oak trees, though large, furnish no suitable timber. In recent years, work has been undertaken on the Hall of Light, and timber has been requisitioned from the various divisions of Qianzhong. Those seeking it have spared no effort. Yet if they failed to assess its quality and mixed in chestnut and oak, what use could it serve? Now, judging scholars by branches measuring mere inches, we find their words forceful and correct, expansive and profound, lucid and possessing an upright substance: here is useful timber. Soon they will find favor with the sagely sovereign, who will allow each to exercise his particular strengths. Not only will their talents merit praise; those conducting this examination will also thereby secure an enduring name. But if their words merely possess ornamental foliage, and we nevertheless confidently [?] recommend them, while in the end they cannot be brought into conformity with established standards or raised into…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
明堂是樗櫟類也在事者將安所
傅其罪乎三代之興有周得
人爲盛仲尼樂議於千載之
下則唐虞首稱蓋壽考作人
非獨以其德懋也亦必久于
其位而後天下化成堯舜是
已當時則稷契皐夔都俞一
===
堂之上此所謂材也彼其靜
言庸違者非樗櫟邪
皇上御極四十年於兹治功煥然
直與唐虞爭烈多士生堯舜
之世且於其身親見之蓋千
載一時也居常自許則唯帝
臣之揖讓何論三代之英乃
punctuated:
明堂，是樗櫟類也。在事者將安所傅其罪乎？三代之興，有周得人爲盛。仲尼樂議於千載之下，則唐虞首稱。蓋壽考作人，非獨以其德懋也，亦必久于其位而後天下化成，堯舜是已。當時則稷契皐夔，都俞一堂之上，此所謂材也。彼其靜言庸違者，非樗櫟邪？
皇上御極四十年於兹，治功煥然，直與唐虞爭烈。多士生堯舜之世，且於其身親見之，蓋千載一時也。居常自許，則唯帝臣之揖讓，何論三代之英？乃
translation_en:
…the Hall of Light: these are of the same kind as the useless ailanthus and oak. Upon whom, then, could those in charge lay the blame? In the rise of the Three Dynasties, Zhou was preeminent in obtaining worthy men. Yet when Zhongni delighted in discussing antiquity a thousand years later, he gave first praise to Tang and Yu, the ages of Yao and Shun. For nurturing men over a long life depends not solely upon abundant virtue: one must also remain long in office before the transformation of all under Heaven can be accomplished. Yao and Shun exemplify this. In their time, Ji, Xie, Gao, and Kui exchanged words of counsel and assent in the same hall. These were what we call men of talent. Those whose words were fine at leisure but whose conduct was contrary—were they not ailanthus and oak?
His Majesty has now occupied the throne for forty years. His achievements in government shine brilliantly, directly rivaling the glories of Tang and Yu. You scholars have been born into an age of Yao and Shun and have personally witnessed it: this is truly an opportunity that comes once in a thousand years. In your customary estimation of yourselves, you aspire only to the ceremonial courtesy of the sage emperors’ ministers; why even speak of the outstanding men of the Three Dynasties? Yet…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
今挾筴而干有司且以言揚
矣他日之所以自獻其身者
將安所決筴哉信能操堯舜
之道以往而無忘其平生之
言則唐虞諸臣將不得專美
於前矣豈惟在事者可幸無
罪而以人事君之義其殆庶
===
幾乎是役也總督兵部右侍
郎兼右僉都御史今陞工部
右侍郎黃光昇飭吏詰戎揚
休錫類頃以代行總督右副
都御史董威舊按茲土風猷
尚在適以代至總督採辦大
木左副都御史李憲卿統攝
punctuated:
今挾筴而干有司，且以言揚矣。他日之所以自獻其身者，將安所決筴哉？信能操堯舜之道以往，而無忘其平生之言，則唐虞諸臣將不得專美於前矣。豈惟在事者可幸無罪，而以人事君之義，其殆庶幾乎！
是役也，總督兵部右侍郎兼右僉都御史、今陞工部右侍郎黃光昇，飭吏詰戎，揚休錫類，頃以代行。總督右副都御史董威，舊按茲土，風猷尚在，適以代至。總督採辦大木左副都御史李憲卿，統攝
translation_en:
…now, bearing their written responses, they seek recognition from the responsible officials and are about to be advanced on the strength of their words. When, in days to come, they offer themselves for service, what course will they resolve upon? If they can truly proceed by the Way of Yao and Shun, without forgetting the words they have professed throughout their lives, then the ministers of Tang and Yu will no longer enjoy exclusive renown for excellence in the past. Not only may those administering this examination hope to escape blame; they may also come close to fulfilling the duty of serving their sovereign by finding worthy men!
For this examination, Huang Guangsheng, Supreme Commander, Right Vice Minister of War, and concurrently Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, now promoted to Right Vice Minister of Works, disciplined the officials, put military affairs in order, fostered excellence, and extended blessings to others. Recently he departed upon being relieved [?]. Dong Wei, Supreme Commander and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, had formerly served as an inspector in this territory, where the influence of his exemplary governance still remained; he arrived at this time as Huang’s replacement. Li Xianqing, Left Vice Censor-in-chief and Supreme Commander overseeing the procurement of large timber, exercised overall supervision…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
三省率曁聲教巡撫右副都
御史今陞南京大理寺卿鮑
〔道明〕拊循綏戢闡猷宣化士
風益振巡撫右僉都御史趙
〔鉞〕方膺
新命撫巡玆鎮工部郎中李〔佑〕刑
部員外郎何〔寵〕工部主事蔣
===
〔弘德〕採木四川按察司副使
王〔有爲〕均有事地方雅重彝
典聿觀厥成若贊襄協志明
謨弼諧則有左參議程〔時思〕
右參議張〔可述〕副使陳〔天賚〕
熊〔勉學〕檢校左右綜理防範
則有署都指揮僉事梁〔高〕楊
punctuated: 三省，率曁聲教。巡撫右副都御史、今陞南京大理寺卿鮑〔道明〕，拊循綏戢，闡猷宣化，士風益振。巡撫右僉都御史趙〔鉞〕，方膺新命，撫巡玆鎮。工部郎中李〔佑〕、刑部員外郎何〔寵〕、工部主事蔣〔弘德〕、採木四川按察司副使王〔有爲〕，均有事地方，雅重彝典，聿觀厥成。若贊襄協志，明謨弼諧，則有左參議程〔時思〕、右參議張〔可述〕、副使陳〔天賚〕、熊〔勉學〕。檢校左右，綜理防範，則有署都指揮僉事梁〔高〕、楊
translation_en:
…the three provinces, bringing them all within the reach of imperial instruction. Bao Daoming 鮑道明, Grand Coordinator and Right Vice Censor-in-chief, now promoted to Minister of the Court of Judicial Review at Nanjing, has comforted and cared for the people, maintained peace and order, expounded imperial policies, and spread the transforming influence of government, further invigorating the ethos of the scholars. Zhao Yue 趙鉞, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-chief, has just received a new appointment to oversee and pacify this command. Li You 李佑, Director in the Ministry of Works; He Chong 何寵, Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice; Jiang Hongde 蔣弘德, Secretary in the Ministry of Works; and Wang Youwei 王有爲, Vice Commissioner of the Sichuan Provincial Surveillance Commission charged with procuring timber, all had official business in the locality. They deeply esteemed this established institution and witnessed its successful completion.

Those who assisted in the undertaking with a common purpose, offering sound counsel and harmonious support, included Cheng Shisi 程時思, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner; Zhang Keshu 張可述, Right Assistant Administration Commissioner; and Vice Surveillance Commissioners Chen Tianlai 陳天賚 and Xiong Mianxue 熊勉學. Those who inspected matters on all sides and oversaw security precautions included Liang Gao 梁高, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, and Yang…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
均至於左叅政羅時霖署都
指揮僉事楊楚共事經始與
有勞勩以入
賀行鎮守總兵官都督同知石
邦憲分守思石右叅將汪輔
楊威戒嚴振武翼文士藉以
寧宇於法得書云
===
直隸徽州府黟縣儒學教諭
陳綵謹序
punctuated:
均。至於左叅政羅時霖、署都指揮僉事楊楚，共事經始，與有勞勩，以入賀行。鎮守總兵官都督同知石邦憲、分守思石右叅將汪輔，楊威戒嚴，振武翼文，士藉以寧宇，於法得書云。

直隸徽州府黟縣儒學教諭陳綵謹序。
translation_en:
…Jun. As for Luo Shilin, Administration Vice Commissioner of the Left, and Yang Chu, Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner, they worked together on the initial arrangements and shared in the toil, before departing to offer congratulations at court. Shi Bangxian, the Regional Commander stationed here and Vice Commissioner-in-Chief, and Wang Fu, Assistant Regional Commander of the Right assigned to defend Si and Shi, displayed their might [?] and maintained strict vigilance, strengthening military preparedness and supporting literary pursuits. Thanks to them, the scholars enjoyed peaceful surroundings. By the conventions of recording events, their contributions merit inclusion here.

Preface respectfully composed by Chen Cai, Instructor of the Confucian School of Yi County, Huizhou Prefecture, in the Directly Administered Region.

收掌試卷官：

黎平府知府張廷桂〔子秀，江西浮梁縣人，庚子貢士〕。

受卷官：
貴州等處提刑按察司經歷司知事孫江〔永卿，直隷定遠縣人，武進縣人，監生〕。

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者樂仁者壽
辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬
禹疏九河瀹濟漯而注諸海決汝漢排淮
泗而注之江
易經
先天而天弗違後天而奉天時
鼎有實慎所之也
===
盛德大業至矣哉
物相遇而後聚故受之以萃萃者聚也聚
而上者謂之升故受之以升
書經
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
羽畎夏翟嶧陽孤桐泗濱浮磬
惟周公克慎厥始惟君陳克和厥中惟公
克成厥終
出入起居罔有不欽
punctuated:
第壹場

四書
知者樂，仁者壽。
辟如天地之無不持載，無不覆幬。
禹疏九河，瀹濟漯而注諸海，決汝漢，排淮泗而注之江。

易經
先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。
鼎有實，慎所之也。
盛德大業，至矣哉！
物相遇而後聚，故受之以萃。萃者，聚也。聚而上者謂之升，故受之以升。

書經
帝光天之下，至于海隅蒼生。
羽畎夏翟，嶧陽孤桐，泗濱浮磬。
惟周公克慎厥始，惟君陳克和厥中，惟公克成厥終。
出入起居，罔有不欽。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books
The wise are joyful; the benevolent are long-lived.
Like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and bear all things and shelter and cover all things.
Yu dredged the Nine Rivers, cleared the Ji and Luo rivers and channeled them into the sea, opened channels for the Ru and Han rivers, and cleared the Huai and Si rivers and channeled them into the Jiang.

Book of Changes (Yijing)
When he acts before Heaven, Heaven does not go against him; when he acts after Heaven, he accords with Heaven’s seasons.
“The cauldron contains food”: he is cautious about where he goes.
Abundant virtue and great achievement—how consummate they are!
Things gather together after encountering one another; therefore, Gathering (Cui) follows. Cui means gathering. Gathering and then moving upward is called rising; therefore, Rising (Sheng) follows.

Book of Documents (Shujing)
The emperor’s radiance spread throughout all beneath Heaven, reaching the people at the shores of the sea.
From the valleys of Yu, the splendidly plumed pheasants; from the southern slope of Yi, the solitary paulownia trees; from the banks of the Si, the exposed stones for musical chimes.
The Duke of Zhou was able to take care at the beginning; Jun Chen was able to maintain harmony in the middle; you, my lord, are able to bring it to completion at the end.
In going out and coming in, in rising and resting, there is nothing in which he is not reverent.

translation_en:
Book of Odes (Shijing)

Gather, gather the plantain; let us pick it. Gather, gather the plantain; let us take it home.

The spring days are long; plants and trees flourish. Orioles sing in harmony; those gathering white southernwood come in throngs.

They seized captives for questioning and captured the enemy throng; then they returned home. Illustrious was Nan Zhong: the Xianyun were subdued.

May the lord live ten thousand years; may you be aided with radiant glory.

He brings peace to the myriad states and abundant harvests year after year.

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

The army of Qi relocated the inhabitants of Ping, Zi, and Wu in Ji. First year of Duke Zhuang.

In summer, in the sixth month, on the yimao day, Xun Linfu of Jin led an army into battle against the Viscount of Chu at Bi. Twelfth year of Duke Xuan. In autumn, a military hunt was held at Hong. Eighth year of Duke Zhao.

Wu attacked Tan. Seventh year of Duke Cheng. The duke met the Marquis of Jin and the Viscount of Wu at Huangchi. Twelfth year of Duke Ai.

In the fifth month, the duke joined the regional lords in a covenant at Gaoyou. Fourth year of Duke Ding.

Book of Rites (Liji)

Examine the rites, rectify punishments, and unify moral conduct in order to honor the Son of Heaven.

By taking Heaven and Earth as the foundation, all things can be brought within its compass.

Manifest the radiance of the highest virtue and set in motion the harmonious vital energies of the four seasons, thereby revealing the principles of all things.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
問性學之明晦關世道之汙隆故韓愈氏
謂孟子性善之說其功不在禹下誠確
論也自是以還微言旣絶横議竝作有
宋諸儒倡明理學各有著述惜在當時
未盡崇信惟我
成祖文皇帝特命儒臣采輯成書名曰性理大
全
親灑
宸翰序諸篇首其曰
===
議論格言輔翼經書有裨斯道曰廣大悉備
如江河之有源委山川之有條理聖賢之道
燦然復明何深嘉而樂與之若斯也今其書
具在試相與評之正蒙一書視之六經
能無少雜乎皇極經世準之六經能無
牽合乎律呂新書果可續古樂之殘缺
否乎洪範內篇果可發箕疇之要訣否
乎我
成祖聖學源流承前啓後所謂爲往古繼絶學
punctuated: 問：性學之明晦，關世道之汙隆。故韓愈氏謂孟子性善之說，其功不在禹下，誠確論也。自是以還，微言旣絶，横議竝作。有宋諸儒倡明理學，各有著述，惜在當時未盡崇信。惟我成祖文皇帝特命儒臣采輯成書，名曰《性理大全》，親灑宸翰，序諸篇首。其曰：「議論格言，輔翼經書，有裨斯道。」曰：「廣大悉備，如江河之有源委，山川之有條理，聖賢之道燦然復明。」何深嘉而樂與之若斯也？今其書具在，試相與評之：《正蒙》一書，視之六經，能無少雜乎？《皇極經世》，準之六經，能無牽合乎？《律呂新書》，果可續古樂之殘缺否乎？《洪範內篇》，果可發箕疇之要訣否乎？我成祖聖學源流，承前啓後，所謂爲往古繼絶學
translation_en:
Question: Whether the learning of human nature is illuminated or obscured bears upon the decline or flourishing of the moral order. Thus Han Yu said that the contribution made by Mengzi’s doctrine of the goodness of human nature was no less than that of Yu. This is indeed a sound judgment. Thereafter, the subtle teachings ceased to be transmitted, and wayward arguments arose together. The Confucian scholars of the Song promoted and elucidated the learning of principle, each producing writings. Regrettably, in their own time they did not receive full esteem and acceptance. Our Emperor Chengzu Wen specially commanded his Confucian officials to gather and compile these writings into a book, entitled the Great Compendium of Human Nature and Principle (Xingli daquan). With his own imperial brush, he wrote a preface to stand at the beginning of the work. In it he said: “Their discussions and exemplary sayings support the Classics and benefit this Way.” He also said: “Vast and fully comprehensive, like rivers with their sources and courses, and mountains and waterways with their ordered patterns, the Way of the sages and worthies shines brightly once again.” Why did he praise them so deeply and endorse them so gladly?

These books are all available today; let us attempt to assess them. When Correcting the Unenlightened (Zhengmeng) is compared with the Six Classics, can it be entirely free of admixture? When Supreme Principles for Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi) is measured against the Six Classics, can it be free of strained correspondences? Can the New Book on Pitch Standards (Lülü xinshu) truly make good what is missing from ancient music? Can the Inner Chapters on the Great Plan (Hongfan neipian) truly reveal the essential teachings of Jizi’s categories? In the origins and transmission of his sagely learning, our Chengzu inherited what came before and opened the way for what followed—what is called continuing the severed tradition of learning from antiquity…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
為萬世開太平者於宋儒之所撰述獨
採擇不遺其
淵衷微妙未易窺測而
謨訓在人可得而述其槩乎我
皇上緝熙性學如
敬一有箴
五箴有註光昭載籍同符
聖祖丕顯丕承萬世爲憲爾諸生涵濡而佩服
之久矣願摘所見聞與六經契合者鋪
張而揚厲之以彰
聖學之萬一
===
問儒者品題人物必中持衡非徒隨聲附
和也試舉一二與諸士商之老氏墨氏
世以爲異論也漢代諸儒世以爲未聞
道也然孔子問禮至稱其爲龍韓愈又
以孔墨竝稱此何謂也漢人傳經史氏
列諸儒林至宋儒註書每援引以取信
此又何也令二氏之書兩漢之文十三
punctuated:
為萬世開太平者，於宋儒之所撰述，獨採擇不遺。其淵衷微妙，未易窺測，而謨訓在人，可得而述其槩乎？我皇上緝熙性學，如《敬一》有箴，《五箴》有註，光昭載籍，同符聖祖，丕顯丕承，萬世爲憲。爾諸生涵濡而佩服之久矣，願摘所見聞與六經契合者，鋪張而揚厲之，以彰聖學之萬一。

問：儒者品題人物，必中持衡，非徒隨聲附和也。試舉一二，與諸士商之。老氏、墨氏，世以爲異論也；漢代諸儒，世以爲未聞道也。然孔子問禮，至稱其爲龍；韓愈又以孔墨竝稱，此何謂也？漢人傳經，史氏列諸儒林，至宋儒註書，每援引以取信，此又何也？令二氏之書、兩漢之文、十三
translation_en:
…and opened an age of great peace for ten thousand generations, gave particular attention to selecting from the writings of the Song Confucians, overlooking none. His profound intentions were subtle and not easily fathomed; yet his counsels and teachings remain among us. Can their general import be recounted? Our present Emperor continually illuminates the learning of human nature: he has composed an admonition on Reverence for the One (Jing yi) and annotations to the Five Admonitions (Wu zhen). These illuminate the written tradition and accord with the sage ancestor. Gloriously manifesting and continuing that legacy, they furnish a model for ten thousand generations. You students have long been steeped in these teachings, cherishing and putting them into practice. Please select from what you have seen and heard those points that accord with the Six Classics, and expound and extol them, thereby revealing some small portion of His Majesty’s sagely learning.

Question: When Confucian scholars appraise people, they must hold the scales impartially, rather than merely echo others’ opinions. Let us raise one or two examples for discussion with you gentlemen. The teachings of Laozi and Mozi are commonly regarded as heterodox, and the Confucian scholars of the Han dynasty as never having heard the Way. Yet Confucius consulted Laozi about ritual and even called him a dragon; Han Yu, moreover, spoke of Confucius and Mozi together. What does this mean? Han scholars transmitted the Classics, and historians included them in the biographies of Confucian scholars. Even Song Confucians, when annotating books, frequently cited them to lend authority to their interpretations. Why was this? Now [?], the books of those two masters, the writings of the two Han dynasties, and the Thirteen …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
經之疏皆在其有背於聖言者歟夫不
察其操心立言之極而肆爲臧否此與
觀場捫燭之見何殊諸生博覽羣籍願
昌言之因以自鏡焉
問兵者聖王不得已而用之者也自軒轅
氏涿鹿之戰下迨唐虞三代皆所不廢
然有曰兵法有曰兵制如黃帝五陣太
公三陣風氏孫臏吳起武侯皆有八陣
李靖有六花陣十二陣周禮大司馬九
===
伐之法孫子九地之術晁錯之所謂五
技孔明之所謂五習是皆禦侮之不可
不知者其義抑可言歟又如漢有八校
隋有十二衛唐有三衛六軍十六衛宋
有三衙四廂十衛是皆屏翰之不可不
講者其制抑可考歟歷代之沿革古今
之優劣抑又有可指議者歟文經武緯
儒者事也願以請纓之志著之篇末
問儒者談經咸謂先王經世之法周禮具
punctuated:
經之疏皆在，其有背於聖言者歟？夫不察其操心立言之極，而肆爲臧否，此與觀場捫燭之見何殊？諸生博覽羣籍，願昌言之，因以自鏡焉。
問：兵者，聖王不得已而用之者也。自軒轅氏涿鹿之戰，下迨唐虞三代，皆所不廢。然有曰兵法，有曰兵制。如黃帝五陣、太公三陣，風氏、孫臏、吳起、武侯皆有八陣，李靖有六花陣、十二陣，《周禮》大司馬九伐之法，《孫子》九地之術，晁錯之所謂五技，孔明之所謂五習，是皆禦侮之不可不知者，其義抑可言歟？又如漢有八校，隋有十二衛，唐有三衛、六軍、十六衛，宋有三衙、四廂、十衛，是皆屏翰之不可不講者，其制抑可考歟？歷代之沿革，古今之優劣，抑又有可指議者歟？文經武緯，儒者事也。願以請纓之志，著之篇末。
問：儒者談經，咸謂先王經世之法，《周禮》具
translation_en:
…the commentaries on the Classics are all extant. Do any of them depart from the words of the sages? If one pronounces praise and blame at will without examining the ultimate purposes underlying their intentions and statements, how does such understanding differ from watching a performance without understanding it or identifying something by feeling a candle? You students have read widely among the books; please speak fully on this, so that I too may use your words as a mirror for self-examination.
Question: Warfare is something to which sage kings resort only when compelled. From Xuanyuan’s battle at Zhuolu down through the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties, none dispensed with it. Yet there are what we call methods of warfare and what we call military institutions. Consider the Yellow Emperor’s five formations and the Grand Duke’s three formations; Feng [?], Sun Bin, Wu Qi, and the Martial Marquis each had eight formations, while Li Jing had the six-flower formation and twelve formations. There are also the Grand Minister of War’s methods of the nine punitive expeditions in the Rites of Zhou, the techniques for the nine kinds of terrain in Master Sun’s Art of War, what Chao Cuo called the five skills, and what Kongming called the five exercises. These are all things one must know to repel aggression. Can you explain their meanings? Again, the Han had eight colonelcies; the Sui, twelve guards; the Tang, three guards, six armies, and sixteen guards; and the Song, three commands, four divisions, and ten guards. These are all institutions that must be studied as bulwarks of the state. Can their organization be ascertained? Can you also identify and discuss what successive dynasties retained or changed, and the relative merits of ancient and later arrangements? To make civil affairs the warp and military affairs the weft is the work of a Confucian scholar. Please conclude your essay by expressing your resolve to volunteer for service.
Question: When Confucian scholars discuss the Classics, they all say that the former kings’ methods of governing the world are fully set forth in the Rites of Zhou…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
備如井田酌古黃帝夏商之規而極一
代之備鄉遂都鄙之制所以生之者有
道三年六年九年之積所以儲之者有
素是以雖有旱乾水溢民無菜色固也
而又有十二荒政何歟且其所謂散利
是即散所儲以賑之矣其曰蕃樂曰薄
征曰弛役曰緩刑曰除盜賊尤爲荒政
之不可廢者他如去譏舍禁近乎縱眚
禮殺哀近乎簡索鬼多昏近乎誣且瀆
===
凡此皆理之可疑者果皆救荒之急務
歟後世常平義倉之設行之當時民甚
稱便庶幾成周積蓄之遺意矣又有興
營造弛鹽禁蠲租稅罷冗吏縱流民募
入粟放囚租勸出粟招商人飭官吏與
所謂十二政者率多出入豈諸君子傚
周禮而行之抑亦因特而立政乎夫泥
古者過於違世因俗者失之拂經玆欲
酌而行之則吾將安取諸生懷用世之
punctuated: 備。如井田，酌古黃帝夏商之規，而極一代之備。鄉遂都鄙之制，所以生之者有道；三年六年九年之積，所以儲之者有素。是以雖有旱乾水溢，民無菜色，固也。而又有十二荒政，何歟？且其所謂散利，是即散所儲以賑之矣。其曰蕃樂，曰薄征，曰弛役，曰緩刑，曰除盜賊，尤爲荒政之不可廢者。他如去譏、舍禁，近乎縱眚；禮殺哀，近乎簡；索鬼、多昏，近乎誣且瀆。凡此皆理之可疑者，果皆救荒之急務歟？後世常平義倉之設，行之當時，民甚稱便，庶幾成周積蓄之遺意矣。又有興營造、弛鹽禁、蠲租稅、罷冗吏、縱流民、募入粟、放囚租、勸出粟、招商人、飭官吏，與所謂十二政者率多出入。豈諸君子傚《周禮》而行之，抑亦因特而立政乎？夫泥古者過於違世，因俗者失之拂經。玆欲酌而行之，則吾將安取？諸生懷用世之
translation_en:
…are fully provided for. The well-field system, for example, drew upon the ancient arrangements of the Yellow Emperor and the Xia and Shang dynasties, bringing them to the fullest development of its age. The institutions of the townships, outer districts, and metropolitan and outlying domains provided orderly means of production; reserves sufficient for three, six, and nine years ensured that storage was regularly maintained. Thus, even in drought or flood, the people showed no signs of hunger. This is readily understandable. Why, then, were there also twelve famine-relief measures?

What is called “distributing resources” plainly means distributing stored supplies for relief. Restricting music, reducing levies, relaxing labor obligations, mitigating punishments, and eliminating robbers and thieves are especially indispensable measures in a famine. Others, however, such as suspending inspections and lifting prohibitions, seem close to indulging wrongdoing; “ritual, reducing mourning” [?] seems close to excessive simplification; seeking aid from spirits and encouraging marriages seem close to deception and profanation. All these present doubts in principle. Are they really all urgent tasks in relieving famine?

When later generations established ever-normal granaries and charitable granaries, the people of those times greatly praised their usefulness. These perhaps preserved something of the intent behind the storage provisions of the Zhou at its height. There were also such measures as initiating construction projects, relaxing restrictions on salt, remitting taxes, dismissing superfluous officials, allowing displaced people freedom of movement, soliciting grain contributions, “releasing prisoners and rents” [?], encouraging people to make grain available, attracting merchants, and admonishing officials. These mostly differed considerably from the so-called twelve measures. Did the gentlemen responsible act in imitation of the Rites of Zhou, or did they establish policies according to particular circumstances [?]?

Those who cling to antiquity err by departing too far from the needs of their age; those who follow current custom err by contravening the classics. If we now wish to weigh these approaches and put them into practice, what should we adopt? You students harbor aspirations to serve the world…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
志久矣毋徒該曰備荒無善政也
問兵食經世急務貴陽僻在遐陬漢夷雜
處以兵則諸衛戍籍十無一存以食則
地鮮田賦仰給川湖比因銅平增兵防
禦至借官軍額派以資餽餉即邊境晏
然一歲之入尚不足支一歲之用或事
起不意計將安出也頃者容山土酋狀
守備寇施秉窺鎮遠聞我兵興則鼠竄
兵散則豕突或謂宜合三省兵力擣其
===
巢穴或謂衛司兼制徵調爲難川湖頻
年逋負不出謂當割四府司四邊衛以
隸貴不知果可行歟諸生生長是邦籌
之預矣幸悉心正議無讓焉
punctuated:
志久矣，毋徒該曰：「備荒無善政也。」

問：兵食，經世急務。貴陽僻在遐陬，漢夷雜處。以兵，則諸衛戍籍十無一存；以食，則地鮮田賦，仰給川湖。比因銅平增兵防禦，至借官軍額派以資餽餉。即邊境晏然，一歲之入尚不足支一歲之用；或事起不意，計將安出也？頃者容山土酋狀守備，寇施秉，窺鎮遠；聞我兵興則鼠竄，兵散則豕突。或謂宜合三省兵力，擣其巢穴；或謂衛司兼制，徵調爲難。川湖頻年逋負不出，謂當割四府司、四邊衛以隸貴。不知果可行歟？諸生生長是邦，籌之預矣，幸悉心正議，無讓焉。
translation_en:
…have long held this aspiration. Do not merely declare [?]: “There are no sound policies for preparing against famine.”

Question: Troops and provisions are urgent concerns in governing the realm. Guiyang lies in a remote corner, where Han Chinese and non-Han peoples live intermixed. As for troops, not even one in ten of those registered for garrison service in the guards remains; as for provisions, the locality yields little land-tax revenue and depends on supplies from Sichuan and Huguang. Recently, because additional troops were stationed in Tong-Ping (銅平) for defense, it has even been necessary to borrow against the regular military allocations [?] to finance their provisioning. Even when the frontier is peaceful, one year’s revenue is insufficient to meet one year’s expenditure. If trouble should arise unexpectedly, what means could be found to meet it?

Recently, the native chieftain of Rongshan [an unclear action involving the commandant: 狀守備], raided Shibing and cast covetous eyes on Zhenyuan. Hearing that our troops are mobilizing, his forces scurry away like rats; when our troops disperse, they charge out like wild boars. Some say that the forces of the three provinces should be combined to strike at their lairs. Others say that divided jurisdiction over the guards and native offices makes requisitioning and mobilization difficult. Sichuan and Huguang have repeatedly failed over successive years to deliver what they owe. It is proposed that four prefectures or native offices [?] and four frontier guards be detached and placed under Guizhou. Could this actually be carried out? You candidates were born and raised in this region and have surely considered these matters beforehand. Please devote your full attention to offering sound proposals, without holding back.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
知者樂仁者壽
李維祜
同考試官教諭常　批　知仁樂壽體認得聖人聲
□且不拈有常句末方見出更覺精彩可以觀所養矣
考試官教諭陳　批　理達隽永宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳　批　清脫中有莊重
聖人别言知仁之效以其所得之深也夫理相
===
因而至者也知之於樂仁之於壽非其造之深
也而有是乎今夫道一而已知者仁者見之而
各就其性之所近故動也靜也因之而各遂其
情之所向矣然豈無其效乎彼性分之中真樂
咸具故樂也者吾固有之也其或未至是者以
有我之私牿之耳夫惟知者之動初非取必於
樂也而樂自生焉明覺自然觸處皆裕知之境
圓神不倚隨在皆活潑之機內省之餘俯仰無
疚焉遇不足以累之也達觀之下天地與游焉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

知者樂，仁者壽。

李維祜

同考試官教諭常批：知仁樂壽，體認得聖人聲□，且不拈「有常」句，末方見出，更覺精彩，可以觀所養矣。

考試官教諭陳批：理達隽永，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭陳批：清脫中有莊重。

聖人别言知仁之效，以其所得之深也。夫理相因而至者也，知之於樂，仁之於壽，非其造之深也而有是乎？今夫道一而已，知者仁者見之，而各就其性之所近，故動也靜也，因之而各遂其情之所向矣。然豈無其效乎？彼性分之中，真樂咸具，故樂也者，吾固有之也。其或未至是者，以有我之私牿之耳。夫惟知者之動，初非取必於樂也，而樂自生焉。明覺自然，觸處皆裕，知之境圓神不倚，隨在皆活潑之機。內省之餘，俯仰無疚焉，遇不足以累之也。達觀之下，天地與游焉。
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“The wise are joyful; the benevolent are long-lived.”

Li Weihu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chang, Instructor: In treating wisdom, benevolence, joy, and longevity, he has grasped the sage’s voice [?]. Moreover, he does not take up the phrase “having constancy” explicitly; only at the end does it emerge, making the essay still more brilliant. One can discern from this what he has cultivated within himself.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: The principles are clearly conveyed, and the meaning is rich and enduring. This should be recorded as a model.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: Within its clarity and ease there is gravity.

The sage speaks separately of the effects of wisdom and benevolence because of the depth of what their possessors have attained. Now, principles lead from one to another until their results are reached. Could wisdom bring joy and benevolence bring longevity unless their possessors had attained such depth?

The Way is one, and that is all. The wise and the benevolent perceive it, each approaching that to which his nature is closest. Thus, whether in activity or stillness, each follows it and fulfills the inclination of his feelings. Yet could this be without its effects?

Within our allotted nature, true joy is fully present. Joy, therefore, is something we inherently possess. If some have not attained it, this is only because selfish attachment to the self confines them. The activity of the wise does not originally insist upon obtaining joy, yet joy arises of itself. Their luminous awareness is spontaneous; wherever they encounter things, they have ample resources. The realm of their wisdom is rounded and wondrous, without leaning to either side; wherever they are, there is the impulse of vibrant life. Upon examining themselves inwardly, they can look down or up without shame; circumstances cannot burden them. Through their comprehensive vision, they roam in company with Heaven and Earth …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
物不足以蔽之也蓋自其樂也以爲知者之能
適其情也不知動斯不括心逸而日休在知者
亦不得而自知矣性天之運恒久不息故壽也
者亦適得吾常也其有未盡然者以客感之私
戕之耳夫惟仁者之靜初非有期於壽也而壽
自臻焉天眞湛一物累已爲之俱忘成性恒存
太和於斯乎保合至靜之淵源心與之涵而久
焉命之原於天者直養而無害也斯理之未貞
神與之安而固焉分之存乎我者克完而無虧
===
也蓋自其壽也以爲仁者之能得乎天也不知
靜斯有常德純而不已在仁者亦不得而自知
矣由是而知惟知者爲能樂而知至於樂與水
之無滯者一也惟仁者爲能壽而仁至於壽與
山之不騫者一也情之所以異趨也有由然矣
然非所造之各詣其極又何以至是也哉雖然
仁知一理也動靜一原也動而無動靜而無靜
互相爲根如知者而盡性故能至命則固未嘗
不壽也仁者而勝私故能不憂則亦未嘗不樂
punctuated: 物不足以蔽之也。蓋自其樂也，以爲知者之能適其情也，不知動斯不括，心逸而日休，在知者亦不得而自知矣。性天之運恒久不息，故壽也者，亦適得吾常也。其有未盡然者，以客感之私戕之耳。夫惟仁者之靜，初非有期於壽也，而壽自臻焉。天眞湛一，物累已爲之俱忘；成性恒存，太和於斯乎保合。至靜之淵源，心與之涵而久焉，命之原於天者，直養而無害也；斯理之未貞，神與之安而固焉，分之存乎我者，克完而無虧也。蓋自其壽也，以爲仁者之能得乎天也，不知靜斯有常，德純而不已，在仁者亦不得而自知矣。由是而知，惟知者爲能樂，而知至於樂，與水之無滯者一也；惟仁者爲能壽，而仁至於壽，與山之不騫者一也。情之所以異趨也，有由然矣。然非所造之各詣其極，又何以至是也哉？雖然，仁知一理也，動靜一原也。動而無動，靜而無靜，互相爲根。如知者而盡性，故能至命，則固未嘗不壽也；仁者而勝私，故能不憂，則亦未嘗不樂
translation_en: …external things cannot obscure them. Observing their joy, one supposes that the wise are able to satisfy their feelings; one does not realize that through activity they remain unconstrained, their minds at ease and daily flourishing. Even the wise themselves cannot be conscious of how this comes about. The workings of Heaven within our nature endure without cease; thus longevity, too, is simply the attainment of our inherent constancy. Where this is not fully realized, it is only because selfish responses to external stimuli injure it. The stillness of the humane does not originally aim at longevity, yet longevity comes of itself. Their innate genuineness is clear and undivided, and all the burdens of external things are forgotten; their fully realized nature constantly abides, and supreme harmony is thereby preserved intact. The mind immerses itself in the deep source of utmost stillness and endures with it: what Heaven has ordained is nourished with rectitude and suffers no injury. In this principle’s ‘not yet being settled’ [?], the spirit rests securely and becomes firm: the allotment residing within oneself is kept whole and unimpaired. Observing their longevity, one supposes that the humane are able to obtain something from Heaven; one does not realize that through stillness they possess constancy, their virtue pure and unceasing. Even the humane themselves cannot be conscious of how this comes about. From this we know that only the wise can truly rejoice; when wisdom reaches joy, it is one with the unobstructed flow of water. Only the humane can truly attain longevity; when humaneness reaches longevity, it is one with the mountain that does not crumble. There is thus a reason why their feelings tend in different directions. Yet unless each carried their attainment to its utmost point, how could they reach this state? Even so, humaneness and wisdom share one principle, and activity and stillness share one source. In activity there is no activity, and in stillness there is no stillness; each serves as the root of the other. Thus the wise fully realize their nature and can thereby fulfill Heaven’s mandate, so they have never been without longevity; the humane overcome selfishness and can thereby be free from anxiety, so they too have never been without joy…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
也其在夫子疏食水飲樂在其中從心所欲年
彌高而德彌邵然則唯夫子爲仁且知矣
辟如天地之無不持載無不覆幬
許宗德
同考試官教諭梁　批　辟如二字作者率多牽合
文雖反梏𥨸思此篇豐腴而能切理令人三復不厭也
考試官教諭陳　批　深識天地聖人之妙
考試官教諭陳　批　博大可觀
中庸贊聖道之大擬諸造化而無間焉夫覆載
===
萬物而無外天地可謂大也而聖人與之準焉
觀此而後可以語聖道矣子思深得聖道之妙
於私淑之後故贊之也豈不曰仲尼之道參於
天地以形言謂之不異不可也以道言謂之不
同不可也吾嘗獨觀其深矣彼祖述憲章是能
集羣聖之成而帝王之道在夫子矣上律下襲
是能體造化之撰而天地之道在夫子矣夫子
之道之大也辟則天地之無不持載無不覆幬
乎夫地以持載爲職夫子亦持載中人耳若非
punctuated:
也。其在夫子，疏食水飲，樂在其中；從心所欲，年彌高而德彌邵。然則唯夫子爲仁且知矣。

辟如天地之無不持載、無不覆幬。
許宗德

同考試官教諭梁批：「辟如二字，作者率多牽合，文雖反梏𥨸思。此篇豐腴而能切理，令人三復不厭也。」
考試官教諭陳批：「深識天地聖人之妙。」
考試官教諭陳批：「博大可觀。」

中庸贊聖道之大，擬諸造化而無間焉。夫覆載萬物而無外，天地可謂大也，而聖人與之準焉。觀此而後可以語聖道矣。子思深得聖道之妙於私淑之後，故贊之也。豈不曰：仲尼之道參於天地，以形言，謂之不異不可也；以道言，謂之不同不可也。吾嘗獨觀其深矣。彼祖述憲章，是能集羣聖之成，而帝王之道在夫子矣；上律下襲，是能體造化之撰，而天地之道在夫子矣。夫子之道之大也，辟則天地之無不持載、無不覆幬乎！夫地以持載爲職，夫子亦持載中人耳，若非
translation_en:
…indeed. As for the Master, he ate coarse food and drank water, yet found joy therein; he followed his heart’s desires, and as his years increased, his virtue grew ever more exalted. Thus only the Master was both benevolent and wise.

“Like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and carry everything, shelter and cover everything.”
Xu Zongde

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “In handling the two characters meaning ‘like,’ writers generally force the comparison; the writing instead constrains their private reflections [?]. This piece is rich and full, yet closely accords with principle, inviting repeated readings without weariness.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “A profound understanding of the subtle workings of Heaven and Earth and the sage.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Broad and great in scope, and worthy of attention.”

The Doctrine of the Mean praises the greatness of the sagely Way, comparing it to the creative transformations of the cosmos and finding no gap between them. Heaven and Earth shelter and sustain the myriad things, leaving nothing outside: they may indeed be called great. Yet the sage measures up to them. Only after observing this can one speak of the sagely Way. Through learning indirectly from the Master’s legacy, Zisi deeply grasped the subtleties of the sagely Way, and therefore praised it. Does he not in effect say: Zhongni’s Way stands alongside Heaven and Earth? In terms of physical form, one cannot say they are without difference; in terms of the Way, one cannot say they are not the same. I have pondered its depths for myself. His carrying forward the ancestral traditions and taking established models as his standard enabled him to bring together the achievements of all the sages: thus the Way of the emperors and kings resided in the Master. His taking his rule from above and following what lay below enabled him to embody the workings of cosmic transformation: thus the Way of Heaven and Earth resided in the Master. In its greatness, is the Master’s Way not like Heaven and Earth, which sustain and carry everything, shelter and cover everything? Earth has sustaining and carrying as its function; the Master, too, sustains and carries—merely an ordinary person [?]—as though they were not…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
所倫也殊不知聖人之道兼總條貫舉古今上
下之理莫不統會於一人之身而體之有以極
其全是卽地道之含弘光大盡天下萬有之類
莫不該括於奠麗之中而合之有以盡其大蓋
地以其形載天下之物聖人以其心載天下之
理均之各極其盛而相似不違聖人其應地無
疆矣乎夫天以覆幬爲職夫子亦覆幬中人耳
若非其類也殊不知聖人之道包含徧覆舉古
今上下之理莫不體受於一人之心而巍乎莫
===
究其端是卽天道之穹窿峻極盡天下散殊之
類莫不至冒於保合之中而渾乎莫窮其際蓋
天以其神而物不能踰聖人以其心而理不能
外均之各極其至而合一無間聖人其配天行
健矣乎是則以天地辟聖人而聖道之全以昭
以聖人擬天地而天地之大益見矣子思子其
真知聖道者與雖然謂聖人有功於天地亦可
也天地非聖人則無以神參賛位育之功而覆
載亦形耳是吾夫子之生固以爲天地立心也
punctuated: 所倫也。殊不知聖人之道兼總條貫，舉古今上下之理，莫不統會於一人之身，而體之有以極其全。是卽地道之含弘光大，盡天下萬有之類，莫不該括於奠麗之中，而合之有以盡其大。蓋地以其形載天下之物，聖人以其心載天下之理，均之各極其盛，而相似不違，聖人其應地無疆矣乎！夫天以覆幬爲職，夫子亦覆幬中人耳，若非其類也。殊不知聖人之道包含徧覆，舉古今上下之理，莫不體受於一人之心，而巍乎莫究其端。是卽天道之穹窿峻極，盡天下散殊之類，莫不至冒於保合之中，而渾乎莫窮其際。蓋天以其神而物不能踰，聖人以其心而理不能外，均之各極其至，而合一無間，聖人其配天行健矣乎！是則以天地辟聖人，而聖道之全以昭；以聖人擬天地，而天地之大益見矣。子思子其真知聖道者與！雖然，謂聖人有功於天地亦可也。天地非聖人，則無以神參賛位育之功，而覆載亦形耳。是吾夫子之生，固以爲天地立心也。
translation_en:
… comparable to it. Yet this overlooks how the sage’s Way comprehensively unites all its ordered strands. All principles, ancient and modern, above and below, converge in the person of a single man, whose embodiment of them realizes their utmost completeness. This is precisely like the Way of Earth in its capaciousness, breadth, brilliance, and greatness: all the myriad kinds of being under Heaven are embraced within what rests upon and is attached to it, and their union fully realizes its greatness. Earth bears the things of the world through its physical form; the sage bears the principles of the world through his mind. Each equally achieves its fullest abundance, and they resemble one another without discord. Does not the sage thus correspond to Earth in its boundlessness? Heaven’s office is to cover and shelter, while the Master is merely one of those beneath its shelter, seemingly not of the same order. Yet this overlooks how the sage’s Way embraces everything and extends its shelter everywhere. All principles, ancient and modern, above and below, are embodied and received within the mind of a single man, so lofty that no one can fathom their ultimate source. This is precisely like the Way of Heaven in its vaulted height and supreme elevation: all the diverse kinds of being under Heaven are reached and covered [?] within its preserving harmony, forming a whole whose bounds cannot be exhausted. Through Heaven’s spiritual efficacy, nothing can pass beyond it; through the sage’s mind, no principle can lie outside it. Each equally reaches its utmost perfection, and they unite without any separation. Does not the sage thus match Heaven in the vigor of its movement? Thus, when Heaven and Earth are used to illustrate the sage, the completeness of the sage’s Way becomes manifest; when the sage is compared to Heaven and Earth, their greatness becomes still more apparent. Master Zisi truly understood the sage’s Way!

Nevertheless, it is also permissible to say that the sage renders service to Heaven and Earth. Without the sage, Heaven and Earth would have no means of bringing spiritual efficacy to the work of participating in and assisting their transformations, setting things in their proper places, and nurturing them; their covering and bearing would be merely physical. Thus, our Master was indeed born to establish a mind for Heaven and Earth.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
夫何叔孫武叔之輩以生井之見乃相與毀之
故子貢解之曰仲尼日月也卽子貢與中庸之
言合而觀之而聖同天地不其然乎
禹疏九河瀹濟漯而注諸海決汝漢排淮
泗而注之江
朱應旌
同考試官教諭黃　批　春容雅淡不事穿鑿誠若
觀河洛而有得者
考試官教諭陳　批　瑩潔可誦佳士也
考試官教諭陳　批　有本之學
===
大賢備舉聖人之治水亦因其勢而導之也蓋
江海者水之所會也聖人治水而悉歸於是焉
其憂民之大亦可見矣孟子闢許行竝耕之論
以曉陳相意謂天下本有當務之急而夫人好
爲立異之說以未聞聖人之道耳彼以堯之憂
爲己憂者舜也而以司空任諸禹視民之溺猶
己溺者禹也而以水土修其職是故天下皆水
也而海爲之壑自洪水之逆行而不注于海斯
punctuated:
夫何叔孫武叔之輩，以生井之見，乃相與毀之？故子貢解之曰：「仲尼日月也。」卽子貢與中庸之言合而觀之，而聖同天地，不其然乎？

「禹疏九河，瀹濟漯而注諸海，決汝漢，排淮泗而注之江。」
朱應旌

同考試官教諭黃批：「春容雅淡，不事穿鑿，誠若觀河洛而有得者。」
考試官教諭陳批：「瑩潔可誦，佳士也。」
考試官教諭陳批：「有本之學。」

大賢備舉聖人之治水，亦因其勢而導之也。蓋江海者，水之所會也。聖人治水而悉歸於是焉，其憂民之大亦可見矣。孟子闢許行竝耕之論，以曉陳相，意謂天下本有當務之急，而夫人好爲立異之說，以未聞聖人之道耳。彼以堯之憂爲己憂者，舜也，而以司空任諸禹；視民之溺猶己溺者，禹也，而以水土修其職。是故天下皆水也，而海爲之壑。自洪水之逆行而不注于海，斯……
translation_en:
Why, then, did men like Shusun Wushu, with their narrow, well-bound understanding [?], join together in disparaging him? Zigong therefore explained: “Zhongni is the sun and moon.” If we consider Zigong’s words together with those of the Doctrine of the Mean, is it not indeed true that the sage equals Heaven and Earth?

“Yu dredged the Nine Rivers, cleared the Ji and Ta rivers and channeled them into the sea, opened channels for the Ru and Han rivers, and cleared the Huai and Si rivers and channeled them into the Yangzi.”
Zhu Yingjing

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: “Graceful and serene, refined and restrained, without forced interpretations: he truly seems to have gained understanding from contemplating the Yellow and Luo rivers.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Limpid and polished, worthy of recitation. A fine scholar.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Learning with a firm foundation.”

The great worthy fully recounts how the sage controlled the waters: he too guided them according to their natural tendencies. The Yangzi and the sea are where waters converge. In controlling the waters, the sage directed them all to these destinations; here we can also see the greatness of his concern for the people. Mencius refuted Xu Xing’s argument that rulers should cultivate the fields alongside their subjects, in order to enlighten Chen Xiang. His meaning was that the world has urgent tasks that demand attention, and that this man delighted in advancing divergent doctrines only because he had never heard the Way of the sages. It was Shun who took Yao’s concerns as his own and entrusted Yu with the office of Minister of Works. It was Yu who regarded the people’s drowning as though he himself were drowning and fulfilled his office by putting the waters and lands in order. Thus, throughout the world there is water, and the sea serves as its receptacle. When the floodwaters flowed against their proper course and failed to discharge into the sea, then…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
無以通其塞民未免於昏墊矣禹則以兗州之
水有九河焉有濟漯焉而疏之瀹之自徒駭以
至鬲津若其朝宗之性導王屋以達枝流適其
統會之區其源不同同歸于海矣蓋海者水之
宗也况九河濟漯又近于海者乎天下皆水也
而江爲之匯自洚水之横流而不注於江斯無
以順其勢民難免於昏溺矣禹則以徐州荊州
之水有汝漢焉有淮泗焉而決之排之導夭息
以及嶓冢得其就下之常濬桐柏以及陪尾因
===
其流濕之勢爲派不一一趨于江矣蓋江者瀆
之大也况汝漢淮泗又近于江者乎夫疏瀹決
排順其自然繼舜而治得其大體所以九州攸
同無懷山襄陵之慮四隩旣宅有地平天成之
休聖人存心天下若此而奚暇於耕哉抑許行
之論固非中正之道然后稷亦有事稼穡何也
蓋民以食爲天聖人以養道教之爾而未始親
之也故曰后稷天下之爲烈也豈一手一足哉
雖然術可以訣聞動衆而甘自食其力行可以
punctuated: 無以通其塞，民未免於昏墊矣。禹則以兗州之水，有九河焉，有濟漯焉，而疏之瀹之。自徒駭以至鬲津，若其朝宗之性；導王屋以達枝流，適其統會之區。其源不同，同歸于海矣。蓋海者，水之宗也，况九河濟漯又近于海者乎？天下皆水也，而江爲之匯。自洚水之横流而不注於江，斯無以順其勢，民難免於昏溺矣。禹則以徐州荊州之水，有汝漢焉，有淮泗焉，而決之排之。導夭息以及嶓冢，得其就下之常；濬桐柏以及陪尾，因其流濕之勢。爲派不一，一趨于江矣。蓋江者，瀆之大也，况汝漢淮泗又近于江者乎？夫疏瀹決排，順其自然，繼舜而治，得其大體，所以九州攸同，無懷山襄陵之慮；四隩旣宅，有地平天成之休。聖人存心天下若此，而奚暇於耕哉？抑許行之論固非中正之道，然 ப后稷亦有事稼穡，何也？蓋民以食爲天，聖人以養道教之爾，而未始親之也。故曰：「后稷天下之爲烈也，豈一手一足哉？」雖然，術可以訣聞動衆，而甘自食其力；行可以
translation_en:
…there would be no way to clear the obstruction, and the people would remain engulfed by the flood. Yu therefore dredged and cleared the waters of Yanzhou—the Nine Rivers and the Ji and Ta rivers. From the Tuhai to the Gejin, he followed their natural tendency to pay homage to the sea; directing the waters from Mount Wangwu through their branches, he guided them to their common gathering place. Though their sources differed, they all returned to the sea. For the sea is where the waters converge; how much more so for the Nine Rivers and the Ji and Ta, which are close to it!

Water covered all the land, and the Yangzi served as its gathering place. When the floodwaters spread unchecked instead of flowing into the Yangzi, there was no way to guide their momentum, and the people could hardly escape drowning. Yu therefore opened channels and drained the waters of Xuzhou and Jingzhou—the Ru and Han, the Huai and Si. He channeled the waters from Yaoxi [?] to Mount Bozhong, allowing them their constant tendency to descend; he dredged from Mount Tongbai to Mount Peiwei, following their tendency to flow toward wet ground. Their channels were many, yet all made their way to the Yangzi. For the Yangzi is the greatest of the principal rivers; how much more so for the Ru, Han, Huai, and Si, which are close to it!

By dredging, clearing, opening channels, and draining, he followed the natural course of the waters. Succeeding Shun in bringing order, he grasped the essential principles. Thus the Nine Provinces were brought into harmony, free from the fear of waters surrounding mountains and overtopping hills; the four corners of the land became habitable, enjoying the blessings of the earth brought to order and Heaven’s work accomplished. With the sage so intent upon the welfare of all under Heaven, what leisure had he for farming?

Yet although Xu Xing’s teaching certainly departed from the correct and balanced Way, Hou Ji also concerned himself with sowing and reaping. Why was this? Because the people regard food as Heaven, the sage taught them the means of sustenance; he did not himself undertake the work. Thus it is said: “Hou Ji’s accomplishments for all under Heaven were vast [?]; could they have been achieved with just one hand and one foot?” Nevertheless, though his methods could win him renown [?] and sway the multitude, he was content to live by his own labor; his conduct could…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
千千乘而不爲苟祿若許行者要亦非凡民也
已
易
先天而天弗違後天而奉天時
饒養浩
同考試官教諭梁　批　講先天後天處頗多語錄
而義晦此作發揮明白錄之
考試官教諭陳　批　詞理明潔蓋究心於易者
考試官教諭陳　批　得旨
===
大人之於天會先後而協於一焉蓋道原於天
而大人則體道者也天人之際夫何先後之有
間哉文言申乾九五爻義及此以爲大人之於
天地日月四時鬼神固無所不合矣然天則無
所不包也大人之於天又何如耶彼天載妙於
玄微元化運於冲漠大人固必先天以有爲也
裁成輔相凡制作以創始者孰非闡神化以肇
其機彌綸範圍凡顯設以開先者孰非立法象
以啓其秘如畫卦以前用未畫之易於是而昭
punctuated:
千千乘而不爲苟祿，若許行者，要亦非凡民也已。

易
先天而天弗違，後天而奉天時。
饒養浩
同考試官教諭梁批：講先天後天處，頗多語錄而義晦，此作發揮明白，錄之。
考試官教諭陳批：詞理明潔，蓋究心於易者。
考試官教諭陳批：得旨。

大人之於天，會先後而協於一焉。蓋道原於天，而大人則體道者也。天人之際，夫何先後之有間哉？文言申乾九五爻義，及此，以爲大人之於天地、日月、四時、鬼神，固無所不合矣。然天則無所不包也，大人之於天又何如耶？彼天載妙於玄微，元化運於冲漠，大人固必先天以有爲也。裁成輔相，凡制作以創始者，孰非闡神化以肇其機？彌綸範圍，凡顯設以開先者，孰非立法象以啓其秘？如畫卦以前，用未畫之易，於是而昭
translation_en:
…approach a ruler of a thousand chariots [?] without seeking an unprincipled livelihood from office. Someone like Xu Xing, after all, was no ordinary man.

Book of Changes
“Acting before Heaven, he encounters no opposition from Heaven; acting after Heaven, he accords with Heaven’s seasons.”
Rao Yanghao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “Explanations of ‘before Heaven’ and ‘after Heaven’ contain many quotations from recorded sayings, yet leave the meaning obscure. This composition expounds it clearly; include it.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “The language and reasoning are clear and polished. The author has evidently devoted himself to studying the Changes.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “It grasps the essential meaning.”

In his relation to Heaven, the great man brings together what comes before and what comes after, harmonizing them as one. For the Way originates in Heaven, and the great man embodies the Way. In the relationship between Heaven and man, how could precedence or succession create any separation? The Commentary on the Words of the Text (Wenyan), elaborating the meaning of the nine in the fifth place of Qian, reaches this point: the great man accords in every respect with Heaven and Earth, the sun and moon, the four seasons, and the spirits. Yet Heaven encompasses everything. What, then, is the great man’s relation to Heaven?

Heaven’s workings are wondrous in their profound subtlety; primordial transformation operates in formless stillness. The great man must indeed act before Heaven to accomplish things. In shaping and completing, assisting and supporting, which of his institutions and innovations does not disclose spiritual transformation and set its workings in motion? In comprehensively ordering and setting bounds, which of his manifest provisions that open the way does not establish models and images to reveal Heaven’s mysteries? For example, before the hexagrams were drawn, he employed the Changes that had not yet been drawn, and thereby made them manifest…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
焉如治曆以明時有過之運於是而成焉天無
心也大人則契天以爲心天何言也大人則代
天以爲言斯則天亦不能不待大人以有爲矣
又豈能違之耶若夫理寓於流行之氣道著於
象形之成大人則後天以奉若也仰觀順承體
天之撰者一皆寅亮以代其工上律時憲順帝
之則者一皆效法以成其能如典自天敘惇之
而爲五典何者非帝畀之良如禮自天秩庸之
而爲五禮何者非天命之正貞觀者天也大人
===
則以之而貞夫一焉無極者天也大人則圖之
而建其極焉斯則大人亦不敢悖天以有爲也
孰非承之而時行耶是則天者大人之體也大
人者天之用也會體用於一原合上下而同流
大人一天矣豈非人之所利見乎抑天之生斯
人也各具一太極者也但衆人梏之而大人能
全之人之利見亦豈徒聖作物覩已耶亦必求
大人之全以復吾之所未全耳故曰有爲者亦
若是希天希聖學易者不可不知
punctuated: 焉。如治曆以明時，有過之運於是而成焉。天無心也，大人則契天以爲心；天何言也，大人則代天以爲言。斯則天亦不能不待大人以有爲矣，又豈能違之耶？若夫理寓於流行之氣，道著於象形之成，大人則後天以奉若也。仰觀順承，體天之撰者，一皆寅亮以代其工；上律時憲，順帝之則者，一皆效法以成其能。如典自天敘，惇之而爲五典，何者非帝畀之良？如禮自天秩，庸之而爲五禮，何者非天命之正？貞觀者天也，大人則以之而貞夫一焉；無極者天也，大人則圖之而建其極焉。斯則大人亦不敢悖天以有爲也，孰非承之而時行耶？是則天者大人之體也，大人者天之用也。會體用於一原，合上下而同流，大人一天矣，豈非人之所利見乎？抑天之生斯人也，各具一太極者也。但衆人梏之，而大人能全之。人之利見，亦豈徒聖作物覩已耶？亦必求大人之全，以復吾之所未全耳。故曰：「有爲者亦若是。」希天希聖，學易者不可不知。
translation_en: …becomes manifest therein. Likewise, by regulating the calendar to clarify the seasons, the cycles of celestial passage [?] are thereby brought to completion. Heaven has no deliberate mind; the great man accords with Heaven and takes it as his mind. What does Heaven say? The great man speaks on Heaven’s behalf. Thus even Heaven must await the great man’s action: how could it oppose him? As for principle residing in the flowing movement of vital force, and the Way becoming manifest in the formation of images and shapes, the great man follows Heaven and obediently accords with it. Looking upward in observation and following reverently, he embodies Heaven’s workings, reverently assisting it and performing its work on its behalf. Taking the seasons above as his rule and following the Supreme Lord’s standards, he invariably models himself upon them to fulfill his capacities. Thus the norms of human relationships derive from Heaven’s ordering: he strengthens them to establish the Five Constant Relationships. Which of them is not a good bestowed by the Supreme Lord? Likewise, ritual derives from Heaven’s ranking: he puts it into practice to establish the Five Rites. Which of them is not the rectitude ordained by Heaven? Heaven displays itself through constancy; the great man draws upon this to hold steadfastly to the One. Heaven is without limit; the great man charts it and establishes the Supreme Ultimate. Thus the great man, too, dares not act contrary to Heaven. Which of his actions does not follow it and proceed at the proper time? Heaven, then, is the substance of the great man, and the great man is Heaven’s functioning. Uniting substance and function in a single source, joining above and below in a common flow, the great man is one with Heaven. Is he not, then, someone whom it is beneficial for people to see? Moreover, when Heaven gives birth to human beings, each possesses a Supreme Ultimate. Ordinary people merely fetter it, whereas the great man can preserve it whole. Can the benefit people gain from seeing him consist merely in the sage’s arising and all beings beholding him? They must also seek the wholeness of the great man, thereby restoring what is not yet whole within themselves. Thus it is said: “One who strives to act can also become like this.” Aspiring to Heaven and aspiring to sagehood—those who study the Book of Changes must understand this.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
盛德大業至矣哉
第一名 許崇德
同考試官教諭梁 批 造化德業發揮殆無餘蘊
似得精微之旨矣取之
考試官教諭陳 批 善言造化之理氣者
考試官教諭陳 批 包達
大傳賛造化之德業而極其妙焉夫天地無心
而成化也則夫德業之著而極其妙也有以哉
大傳論一陰一陽之道及此謂夫道不外於陰
陽而實妙於德業今夫造化之顯諸仁所以鼓
===
萬物之出機也黃鍾起貞下之元有以煥生意
於莫掩槖籥乎寂中之感有以溥化育於咸章
凡庶類之含實理於宥密者莫不揚詡於無外
也德何盛乎及夫造化之藏諸用所以鼓萬物
之入機也太和保合而元氣於是乎其凝性命
各正而真精于斯乎畢聚凡萬有之具實理於
胚胎者莫不完固於無窮也業何大乎夫德言
盛矣業言大矣而或涉於有憂未可以言至也
punctuated:
盛德大業至矣哉！

第一名，許崇德。

同考試官教諭梁批：造化德業，發揮殆無餘蘊，似得精微之旨矣，取之。
考試官教諭陳批：善言造化之理氣者。
考試官教諭陳批：包達。

大傳賛造化之德業而極其妙焉。夫天地無心而成化也，則夫德業之著而極其妙也，有以哉！大傳論一陰一陽之道，及此謂夫道不外於陰陽，而實妙於德業。今夫造化之顯諸仁，所以鼓萬物之出機也。黃鍾起貞下之元，有以煥生意於莫掩；槖籥乎寂中之感，有以溥化育於咸章。凡庶類之含實理於宥密者，莫不揚詡於無外也，德何盛乎！及夫造化之藏諸用，所以鼓萬物之入機也。太和保合，而元氣於是乎其凝；性命各正，而真精于斯乎畢聚。凡萬有之具實理於胚胎者，莫不完固於無窮也，業何大乎！夫德言盛矣，業言大矣，而或涉於有憂，未可以言至也。
translation_en:
“Abundant virtue and great achievement—how consummate they are!”

First place: Xu Chongde.

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “His exposition of the virtue and achievement of cosmic transformation leaves almost nothing unexplored. He seems to have grasped its subtle purport. Accept him.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “One who explains well the principle and material force of cosmic transformation.”
Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Comprehensive and penetrating.”

The Great Commentary praises the virtue and achievement of cosmic transformation, bringing out their utmost subtlety. Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without conscious intention. There is thus a reason why their virtue and achievement become manifest in such consummate subtlety! The Great Commentary discusses the Way of alternating yin and yang; at this point it says that the Way lies nowhere outside yin and yang, yet its true subtlety resides in virtue and achievement.

Now, cosmic transformation manifests itself in benevolence: this is how it sets in motion the workings through which the myriad things emerge. The Yellow Bell pitch initiates the originating force beneath steadfastness, making the impulse of life shine forth irrepressibly. Like bellows, it stirs a response within stillness [?], spreading transformative nurture until all becomes manifest. All the various kinds of beings that contain real principle within profound hiddenness unfold and flourish throughout the boundless whole. How abundant this virtue is!

Then cosmic transformation conceals itself in functioning: this is how it sets in motion the workings through which the myriad things withdraw. Supreme harmony is preserved in union, and primordial material force thereby condenses. Each being’s nature and allotted destiny are set right, and true essence gathers here in its entirety. All the myriad beings that possess real principle in their embryonic state are made complete and secure without end. How great this achievement is!

Yet although virtue is called abundant and achievement great, if either involves any anxious concern, it cannot be called consummate.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
惟夫自靜而動以爲造化之德在是矣殊不知
天地司之天地不得而與之也無思無爲幷其
所謂盛者而忘之矣自動而靜以爲造化之業
在是矣殊不知天地宰之天地不得而知之也
何思何慮幷其所謂大者而化之矣運玄功於
寂若泯意象於俱無信乎無心之妙非有心之
所能及也又何如其至也哉吁於顯仁見道之
行於陽焉於藏用見道之具於陰焉道之體用
不外於陰陽如是夫抑德業一也在天地無心
===
而成化聖人有心而無爲然天地之無心不能
不賴於聖人之有心使非聖人裁成輔相範圍
曲成而天地之德業亦幾乎息矣故雖不與聖
人同憂而聖人之心代天地之憂又安知天地
之心非聖人之心耶
書
帝光天之下至于海隅蒼生
陳一龍

translation_en:
Now, as stillness gives rise to movement, one supposes that the virtue of creation lies herein. Little does one realize that, although Heaven and Earth preside over it, they cannot deliberately intervene in it. Without thought or action, they forget even what is called its abundance. As movement gives way to stillness, one supposes that the achievement of creation lies herein. Little does one realize that, although Heaven and Earth govern it, they cannot consciously know it. What thought, what deliberation is there? Even what is called its greatness dissolves in transformation. They exercise their mysterious efficacy in utter stillness and efface intentions and images in complete absence. Truly, the marvel of acting without deliberate intent is beyond the reach of deliberate intent. How could anything equal its perfection? Ah! In the manifestation of benevolence we see the Way operating in yang; in the concealment of its functioning we see the Way embodied in yin. Thus the substance and functioning of the Way do not extend beyond yin and yang!
Yet virtue and achievement are one. Heaven and Earth accomplish transformation without deliberate intent; the sage possesses intent yet acts without contrivance. Nevertheless, Heaven and Earth's absence of intent must depend upon the sage's possession of intent. Were the sage not to shape and assist their processes, encompass them and bring every particular to fulfillment, the virtue and achievement of Heaven and Earth would all but cease. Thus, although they do not share the sage's cares, the sage's mind bears those cares on behalf of Heaven and Earth. How, then, can we know that the mind of Heaven and Earth is not the mind of the sage?

…In discussing “the common people at the shores of the seas,” he shows particular insight.
Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: “Classical and exemplary.”
Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: “Rigorous and orderly.”
The great minister’s expectation that sagely virtue should manifest itself far and wide serves to emphasize its foundation. Virtue is the foundation for transforming the people. If sagely virtue manifests itself so far afield, can any of the people remain untransformed? The great Yu meant that people’s hearts could be transformed through virtue but could not be coerced through intimidation. If the many obstinate people failed to obey, it was simply because luminous virtue had not yet spread among them. Could the matter simply be left there?
Now, considered as harmony and compliance accumulated within, it is called virtue; considered as virtue issuing outward, it is called radiance. This is the means by which the people are transformed. If the emperor truly grounds it in his own person and verifies it among the common people, his virtue becomes widespread and his transforming influence radiant, brilliantly displaying its manifest pattern. Issuing from what is near and becoming apparent far away, his sincerity is pure and his cultivated virtue luminous, splendidly sending forth the radiance of consummate virtue. When rites and music are clearly established and complete, and Heaven and Earth fulfill their offices [?], the broad dissemination of civil virtue renews itself daily and cannot cease. When the warp and weft of government are patterned and its subtlest workings become apparent, the spreading influence of Chonghua—that is, Shun—is so abundant that nothing can surpass it.
Thus, all under Heaven is vast, and the common people at the shores of the seas are exceedingly distant. When the emperor’s virtue reaches throughout all under Heaven, extending to the common people at the shores of the seas, its greatness leaves nothing outside it: this is greatness at its utmost. In terms of distance, nothing checks its reach: this is remoteness at its furthest extent. Since no land is other than the king’s land, there is nowhere that consummate virtue, profound benevolence, and generous bounty do not reach. Indeed, its expansiveness is such that its furthest extent cannot be fathomed, nor can it be described in terms of limits or measure…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
有望于大臣乎康王命畢公之意以爲更化可
以善治泥古適以病民誠以殷民之治方其始
也世道方降之時政寛則民慢矣非治之善也
是故周公毖殷而謹厥始所以使民易避而難
犯者未嘗不用嚴以治之也世可以嚴則嚴周
公不能不與世推移矣周公何心哉及其中也
世道將升之時政猛則民殘矣非治之善也是
故君陳有容而和厥中所以使民感慕而興起
者未始不用寛以治之也時可以寛則寛君陳
===
不能不與時消息矣君陳何心哉然古今之不
相沿者時也而後先之所相望者治也公其念
剛柔爲保民之道化裁以利其用寛猛爲爲政
之體損益以宜其民不剛以濟周公之剛師其
意不泥其迹務使協心之治有以息未殄之風
治自周公始者亦自公而終之矣不柔以濟君
陳之柔通其變使民不倦務使由俗之政有以
閑未定之心治自君陳中者亦自公以成之矣
至是則世變風移而殊厥井疆不足以擬之矣
punctuated: 有望于大臣乎？康王命畢公之意，以爲更化可以善治，泥古適以病民。誠以殷民之治，方其始也，世道方降之時，政寛則民慢矣，非治之善也。是故周公毖殷而謹厥始，所以使民易避而難犯者，未嘗不用嚴以治之也。世可以嚴則嚴，周公不能不與世推移矣，周公何心哉？及其中也，世道將升之時，政猛則民殘矣，非治之善也。是故君陳有容而和厥中，所以使民感慕而興起者，未始不用寛以治之也。時可以寛則寛，君陳不能不與時消息矣，君陳何心哉？然古今之不相沿者，時也；而後先之所相望者，治也。公其念剛柔爲保民之道，化裁以利其用；寛猛爲爲政之體，損益以宜其民。不剛以濟周公之剛，師其意，不泥其迹，務使協心之治有以息未殄之風，治自周公始者，亦自公而終之矣。不柔以濟君陳之柔，通其變，使民不倦，務使由俗之政有以閑未定之心，治自君陳中者，亦自公以成之矣。至是則世變風移，而殊厥井疆不足以擬之矣。
translation_en:
…look to the great ministers? King Kang’s intention in charging Bi Gong was that reform could bring good government, whereas rigid adherence to antiquity would only harm the people. Indeed, when the governance of the people of Yin first began, the moral condition of the age was declining. Lenient government would have made the people negligent; this would not have been good government. Thus Zhou Gong exercised vigilance over Yin and took care at the outset. In making it easy for the people to avoid wrongdoing and difficult for them to transgress, he invariably governed them with strictness. When the age called for strictness, he was strict: Zhou Gong could not but adapt to the changes of the age. What personal preference did Zhou Gong have in this?

By the middle stage, the moral condition of the age was about to improve. Harsh government would have injured the people; this would not have been good government. Thus Jun Chen showed forbearance and brought harmony to this middle stage. In inspiring the people’s admiration and stirring them to better themselves, he invariably governed them with leniency. When the times called for leniency, he was lenient: Jun Chen could not but adjust to the ebb and flow of the times. What personal preference did Jun Chen have in this?

Yet what differs between antiquity and the present is the times; what predecessors and successors alike expect of one another is good government. You, my lord, should consider firmness and gentleness as means of protecting the people, adapting and tempering them to make their application beneficial; and leniency and severity as the essential modes of government, diminishing or augmenting them to suit the people. Complement Zhou Gong’s firmness by refraining from firmness yourself: emulate his intent without clinging to his precedents. Strive to ensure that government which unites people’s hearts can put an end to customs not yet eradicated. The work of government begun by Zhou Gong will then be brought to completion by you. Complement Jun Chen’s gentleness by refraining from gentleness yourself: carry through the necessary changes so that the people do not grow weary. Strive to ensure that government which follows local customs can restrain hearts not yet settled. The work of government carried forward by Jun Chen in its middle stage will then be perfected by you. At this point, the age will be transformed and customs changed; even the separation of their fields and boundaries would be insufficient to compare with this achievement.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
壽夢親將爲伐郯之舉是伐也將固尊焉者也
致周之族屬則有伯父之稱而乃以號舉何也
蓋在春秋夷狄上下同詞而不分爵號吳於是
時棄本爵而弗居僭王號以自擬是自入於夷
者也故今之伐郯元戎啓行不曰吳師而曰王
師也兵威孔楊不曰君命而曰王命也夫夷而
猾夏已無出入之防不有以黜之何以傾否而
保泰乎故黜而舉號等諸夷也聖人非特爲其
陵夏也爲其僭王也僭王之罪必因伐而始見
===
爾吳至夫差與晉爲黃池之會是會也彼固主
之者也致周之命圭嘗有吳伯之命而猶以子
稱何也蓋在春秋四夷雖大皆曰子吳之先世
冒一王之大號更數世而未革是不能自拔於
夷者也故今之爲會席戰勝之威而凌駕乎晉
室秉驕矜之氣而雄長於諸侯夫霸降而夷固
已拂天地之經不有以抑之何以紀常而正名
乎故抑而稱子視諸夷也聖人非特爲其主會
也爲其無王也無王之罪必因會而益彰嗚乎
punctuated:
壽夢親將爲伐郯之舉。是伐也，將固尊焉者也。致周之族屬，則有伯父之稱，而乃以號舉，何也？蓋在春秋，夷狄上下同詞，而不分爵號。吳於是時，棄本爵而弗居，僭王號以自擬，是自入於夷者也。故今之伐郯，元戎啓行，不曰吳師而曰王師也；兵威孔楊，不曰君命而曰王命也。夫夷而猾夏，已無出入之防，不有以黜之，何以傾否而保泰乎？故黜而舉號，等諸夷也。聖人非特爲其陵夏也，爲其僭王也。僭王之罪，必因伐而始見爾。
吳至夫差，與晉爲黃池之會。是會也，彼固主之者也。致周之命圭，嘗有吳伯之命，而猶以子稱，何也？蓋在春秋，四夷雖大，皆曰子。吳之先世，冒一王之大號，更數世而未革，是不能自拔於夷者也。故今之爲會，席戰勝之威而凌駕乎晉室，秉驕矜之氣而雄長於諸侯。夫霸降而夷，固已拂天地之經，不有以抑之，何以紀常而正名乎？故抑而稱子，視諸夷也。聖人非特爲其主會也，爲其無王也。無王之罪，必因會而益彰。嗚乎！

…Shoumeng personally led the expedition against Tan. In this campaign, the commander was indeed a person of exalted standing. Considering his kinship with the Zhou royal house [?], he was entitled to the designation “senior uncle”; why, then, was he recorded merely by his state's name? In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the same terminology is used for barbarians of higher and lower standing, without distinguishing their noble ranks and titles. At this time, Wu abandoned its proper rank and refused to abide by it, usurping the title of king for itself. It thus placed itself among the barbarians. Hence, in this attack on Tan, when the great war chariots set forth, its forces were called not “the army of Wu” but “the royal army”; when its military might was greatly displayed, its commands were called not “the ruler's commands” but “the king's commands.” When barbarians thus disturb the Chinese states, the boundary between outside and inside has already been lost. Without demoting them, how could one overturn disorder and preserve peace? Thus, recording the ruler merely by his state's name demotes him and places him on a level with the barbarians. The Sage did this not merely because Wu encroached upon the Chinese states, but because it usurped the royal title. The offense of usurping that title first became manifest through the attack.
When Wu reached the reign of Fuchai, it met with Jin at Huangchi. At this meeting, Wu was indeed the presiding party. Considering the jade tablet of investiture bestowed by Zhou [?], there had once been an investiture as Earl of Wu; why, then, was its ruler still styled “viscount”? In the Spring and Autumn Annals, the barbarians of the four quarters, however great, are all styled “viscount.” Wu's ancestors had presumptuously assumed the exalted title of king, and several generations had passed without their abandoning it. They were thus unable to extricate themselves from the ranks of the barbarians. Hence, at this meeting, Wu relied on the prestige of its military victories to overawe the ruling house of Jin, and with arrogant self-importance asserted supremacy over the feudal lords. When the hegemony descends to the barbarians, this already violates the constant order of Heaven and Earth. Without restraining Wu, how could one uphold enduring norms and rectify names? Thus, lowering its ruler to the designation “viscount” treats him as a barbarian. The Sage did this not merely because Wu presided over the meeting, but because it acknowledged no king. The offense of acknowledging no king became still more conspicuous through the meeting. Alas!…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
天下有禮焉諸侯固當遵而行之矣然能必其
無違僭乎則於是考之凡大小顯微之制經曲
隆殺之宜求不乖乎紀法之宗而惟天子所議
斯已矣出自一人而以防範乎天下有刑焉諸
侯固當舉而用之矣然能必其無偏枉乎則於
是正之凡附宥出入之條輕重小大之比求不
失乎明允之當而即天倫以麗事斯已矣本之
吾心以盡事君之義有德焉諸侯非不有是心
也而能不二者鮮矣則從而一焉純乎篤棐之
===
忱而不乘以僞妄之私確乎忠貞之念而無間
於二三之雜蓋以天子之心爲心不自以其心
爲心矣若此者非尊天子乎吾見其則君以自
治而靖共厥職自獻以成信而精白承休考禮
以尊禮也正刑以尊刑也一德以尊德也祇承
欽若無非一王之典而罔敢自外於惟皇之極
者皆自此而見矣竭情盡慎莫非昭事之誠而
罔敢懷二心以事其上者皆於此乎立矣其爲
尊天子也孰大於是是則天子固無事而朝君
punctuated: 天下有禮焉，諸侯固當遵而行之矣。然能必其無違僭乎？則於是考之，凡大小顯微之制、經曲隆殺之宜，求不乖乎紀法之宗，而惟天子所議，斯已矣。出自一人而以防範乎天下，有刑焉，諸侯固當舉而用之矣。然能必其無偏枉乎？則於是正之，凡附宥出入之條、輕重小大之比，求不失乎明允之當，而即天倫以麗事，斯已矣。本之吾心，以盡事君之義，有德焉。諸侯非不有是心也，而能不二者鮮矣，則從而一焉。純乎篤棐之忱，而不乘以僞妄之私；確乎忠貞之念，而無間於二三之雜。蓋以天子之心爲心，不自以其心爲心矣。若此者，非尊天子乎？吾見其則君以自治，而靖共厥職；自獻以成信，而精白承休。考禮以尊禮也，正刑以尊刑也，一德以尊德也。祇承欽若，無非一王之典，而罔敢自外於惟皇之極者，皆自此而見矣。竭情盡慎，莫非昭事之誠，而罔敢懷二心以事其上者，皆於此乎立矣。其爲尊天子也，孰大於是？是則天子固無事而朝君

…throughout all under Heaven, there are rites, which the feudal lords assuredly ought to observe and carry out. Yet can they guarantee that there will be no transgression or usurpation? Thus they examine them: all the regulations concerning great and small matters, the manifest and the subtle, and the appropriate forms for general principles and particular details, elaboration and reduction. They seek only to remain faithful to the guiding principles of order and law and to follow what the Son of Heaven has determined.

There are punishments, issuing from the One Man to restrain all under Heaven, which the feudal lords assuredly ought to apply. Yet can they guarantee that there will be no partiality or injustice? Thus they rectify them: all the provisions for assigning penalties and granting leniency, mitigating and aggravating sentences, and the precedents for offenses light and heavy, small and great. They seek only to preserve the proper balance of discernment and fairness, applying the natural order of human relationships in adjudicating cases.

There is virtue, rooted in one’s own heart, through which one fulfills the duty of serving one’s ruler. It is not that the feudal lords lack this disposition, but few can keep it undivided. Thus they make it single: pure in their sincere commitment to steadfast assistance, without the intrusion of selfish deceit and falsehood; firm in their resolve of loyalty and constancy, without the interference of wavering allegiances. They take the Son of Heaven’s heart as their own, rather than making their own hearts their guide. Is this not honoring the Son of Heaven?

I see them taking their ruler as the standard for governing themselves and respectfully attending to their duties; offering themselves in complete good faith and receiving his beneficence with utter purity. They examine rites to honor rites, rectify punishments to honor punishments, and unify their virtue to honor virtue. Their reverent observance and respectful conformity accord wholly with the statutes of the sovereign; their refusal to place themselves outside the sovereign’s supreme norm is manifested in all these things. Their utmost devotion and care are wholly expressions of sincerity in illustrious service; their refusal to harbor divided loyalty in serving their superior is established through all these things. What could be greater than this in honoring the Son of Heaven? Thus the Son of Heaven, free from the need for intervention, grants audience to the lords…
