title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
聖人之所以益聖也夫道命於天具於心者性
也稽諸古驗諸物理而求諸此心者善學
者也得諸心徵諸行事而見之記載者儒
者事也惟
聖人爲能神而明之故興起乎異世而獨造其
極會通乎百王而獨得其全以之繼往則
心源默契而上下古今由是而貫徹以之
開來則述作兼資而宏綱樞要由是而恢
弘然後知世有升降而性道無絕續見有
異同而性學所由資也我
===
成祖所以博采乎諸儒
皇上所以緝熙乎
聖學愚生庶乎彷彿仰窺其萬一矣請得以所
見聞而掇述之可乎蓋自惟皇降衷若有
恒性見於書而性之名始立繼之者善成
之者性係於易而性之義始著詩有六義
道此者也禮有三百三千節此者也樂有
五聲十二律和此者也春秋大義數十以
punctuated:
聖人之所以益聖也。夫道命於天、具於心者，性也。稽諸古，驗諸物理，而求諸此心者，善學者也。得諸心，徵諸行事，而見之記載者，儒者事也。惟聖人爲能神而明之，故興起乎異世而獨造其極，會通乎百王而獨得其全。以之繼往，則心源默契，而上下古今由是而貫徹；以之開來，則述作兼資，而宏綱樞要由是而恢弘。然後知世有升降，而性道無絕續；見有異同，而性學所由資也。我成祖所以博采乎諸儒，皇上所以緝熙乎聖學，愚生庶乎彷彿仰窺其萬一矣。請得以所見聞而掇述之，可乎？
蓋自「惟皇降衷，若有恒性」見於《書》，而性之名始立；「繼之者善，成之者性」係於《易》，而性之義始著。《詩》有六義，道此者也；《禮》有三百三千，節此者也；《樂》有五聲十二律，和此者也；《春秋》大義數十，以
translation_en:
…is how the sage becomes still more sagely. As for the Way, that which is ordained by Heaven and inherent in the heart is human nature. Those who investigate antiquity, test their understanding against the principles of things, and seek it within their own hearts are skilled in learning. To apprehend it in the heart, substantiate it in conduct and affairs, and give it expression in written records is the work of Confucian scholars. Only the sage can comprehend it with wondrous insight and make it manifest. Thus, arising in a different age, he alone reaches its utmost limit; comprehending what runs through the reigns of a hundred kings, he alone grasps its entirety. In carrying forward the past, he finds silent accord with the source within the heart, thereby achieving an understanding that runs throughout antiquity and the present. In opening the way for the future, he draws upon both transmission and original composition, thereby extending the great framework and its essential principles. Only then do we understand that although ages rise and decline, the Way of human nature suffers no interruption; although views differ or coincide, they provide resources for the study of human nature. Why our Emperor Chengzu gathered widely from the Confucian scholars, and why His Majesty continually illuminates the learning of the sages—of this, I, an ignorant student, may perhaps dimly glimpse one ten-thousandth part as I look up in reverence. May I gather together and recount what I have seen and heard?
When the words “The Sovereign bestowed an inner moral norm, in accordance with which people possess a constant nature” appeared in the Book of Documents, the designation “human nature” was first established. When “What continues it is goodness; what brings it to completion is human nature” was appended to the Book of Changes, the meaning of human nature first became manifest. The Book of Odes has six principles: these give expression to it. The rites have three hundred major rules and three thousand detailed observances: these regulate it. Music has five notes and twelve pitch standards: these harmonize it. The Spring and Autumn Annals has several dozen great principles, by which…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
正名分正此者也故道在天地者具在六
經夫何世遠教湮大義斯乖異論竝作與
正學爭衡於是孟子起而闢之以仁義禮
智證性之善以惻隱羞惡辭讓是非驗性
之端反而求之則爲聖賢之學擴而充之
則爲帝王之治性之爲道昭然矣然而權
謀功利錮蔽人心漢唐以降若韓愈氏且
謂性有三品若歐陽修氏亦謂聖人教人
性非所先他尚何望哉無怪乎性學之日
===
趨於晦也天佑斯文濂洛關閩眞儒輩出
講學窮理著書立言其純乎無以議爲者
周程與朱而已當是時諸儒相與講明性
學各以意見所到著之簡編故學者拘攣
舊聞互相質正其議正蒙則曰清虛一大
涉於空寂也論皇極經世則曰引經引義
別爲一說也樂有六律旋相爲宮而蔡季
通乃以積分候氣變律變徵言之漢儒註
疏爲多也此律呂新書之說也範有九疇
punctuated:
正名分，正此者也。故道在天地者，具在六經。夫何世遠教湮，大義斯乖，異論竝作，與正學爭衡？於是孟子起而闢之，以仁義禮智證性之善，以惻隱羞惡辭讓是非驗性之端。反而求之，則爲聖賢之學；擴而充之，則爲帝王之治。性之爲道，昭然矣。然而權謀功利，錮蔽人心。漢唐以降，若韓愈氏且謂性有三品，若歐陽修氏亦謂聖人教人，性非所先，他尚何望哉！無怪乎性學之日趨於晦也。
天佑斯文，濂洛關閩眞儒輩出，講學窮理，著書立言。其純乎無以議爲者，周程與朱而已。當是時，諸儒相與講明性學，各以意見所到，著之簡編。故學者拘攣舊聞，互相質正。其議《正蒙》，則曰清虛一大涉於空寂也；論《皇極經世》，則曰引經引義，別爲一說也。樂有六律，旋相爲宮，而蔡季通乃以積分候氣、變律變徵言之，漢儒註疏爲多也。此《律呂新書》之說也。《範》有九疇，
translation_en:
…to rectify names and distinctions of status: this is what they set right. Thus the Way present in Heaven and Earth is fully embodied in the Six Classics. How was it that, as the ages grew distant and the teachings fell into obscurity, the great principles were distorted and divergent doctrines arose together to contend with orthodox learning? Thereupon Mengzi arose to refute them. Through benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom, he demonstrated the goodness of human nature; through compassion, shame and aversion, deference and yielding, and the sense of right and wrong, he verified its beginnings. To turn inward and seek these is the learning of sages and worthies; to extend and fully develop them is the government of emperors and kings. Human nature as the Way was thereby made manifest. Yet scheming for power and pursuing achievement and profit fettered and obscured people's minds. From the Han and Tang onward, even Han Yu maintained that human nature had three grades, while Ouyang Xiu likewise maintained that, in teaching people, the sages did not put human nature first. What could one hope for from the others! Little wonder that the study of human nature grew ever more obscure.
Heaven protected this cultural tradition, and true Confucian scholars emerged in succession from Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min. They expounded learning, investigated principles, wrote books, and established teachings. Yet those whose teachings were so pure as to admit of no criticism were only Zhou Dunyi, the Cheng brothers, and Zhu Xi. At that time, the scholars jointly elucidated the study of human nature, each committing to writing what his understanding had reached. Thus scholars, constrained by received learning, questioned and corrected one another. In criticizing Correcting Youthful Ignorance (Zhengmeng), they said that its account of the clear, vacuous, unified, and great verged on emptiness and quiescence. In discussing Supreme Principles for Ordering the World (Huangji jingshi), they said that it cited the classics and drew upon their meanings to construct a separate doctrine. Music has six pitch standards, which take turns serving as the gong, or fundamental tone. Yet Cai Jitong discussed these in terms of accumulating numerical fractions, observing the qi, altering pitch standards, and altering the zhi tone [?], drawing largely upon the annotations and subcommentaries of Han Confucian scholars. Such is the account in the New Book on Pitch Standards (Lülü xinshu). The Great Plan has nine categories…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
其要矣又於宋儒之箴特加註釋在心箴
則以涵養本原之功於斯為切弗以韋布
之學略之也在四箴則以孔顏克復之學
於斯喫緊不以章句之儒忽之也蓋二儒
之作視宋家文字尤為有補於性學故獨
當
聖心揭示學校則是心法愈衍而愈彰
皇上之所以為聖乎採二子之長以昭示性學
於無窮
===
皇上之所以益聖乎所以然者性道之在天下
非聖賢則何以濬其源非宋儒則無以導
其流自諸儒之言出而後之君子因考據
以黜夫似是之非窺門戶以挼夫如綫之
緒彼不覩其全而指摘一二是猶迷波而
忘源也嘗觀之堯矣舜命官禹治水稷司
農契敷教臯陶明刑伯夔典樂岳牧之司
各效其職堯端拱於上而萬邦時雍至頌
堯之為君則曰大哉以堯因才而竝用之
punctuated: 其要矣。又於宋儒之箴，特加註釋。在心箴，則以涵養本原之功於斯為切，弗以韋布之學略之也；在四箴，則以孔顏克復之學於斯喫緊，不以章句之儒忽之也。蓋二儒之作，視宋家文字，尤為有補於性學，故獨當聖心，揭示學校，則是心法愈衍而愈彰。皇上之所以為聖乎！採二子之長，以昭示性學於無窮，皇上之所以益聖乎！所以然者，性道之在天下，非聖賢則何以濬其源？非宋儒則無以導其流。自諸儒之言出，而後之君子因考據以黜夫似是之非，窺門戶以挼夫如綫之緒。彼不覩其全而指摘一二，是猶迷波而忘源也。嘗觀之堯矣：舜命官，禹治水，稷司農，契敷教，臯陶明刑，伯夔典樂，岳牧之司各效其職。堯端拱於上，而萬邦時雍。至頌堯之為君，則曰：「大哉！」以堯因才而竝用之
translation_en:
…its essentials. Moreover, he supplied special annotations to the admonitions of the Song Confucians. In the Admonition on the Mind, he regarded the work of nurturing the fundamental source as especially pertinent here, and did not slight it as the learning of a commoner in plain cloth. In the Four Admonitions, he regarded the learning of Confucius and Yan Hui concerning self-mastery and returning to ritual propriety as urgently relevant here, and did not disregard it as the work of a scholar concerned merely with textual divisions and phrases. Compared with other Song writings, the works of these two scholars are especially beneficial to the study of human nature. Thus they alone found particular favor in the imperial mind and were displayed in the schools; through this, the teaching of the mind has become ever more widely transmitted and more clearly manifest. Is this not what makes His Majesty a sage! Drawing on the strengths of these two masters to illuminate the study of human nature for all time—is this not what makes His Majesty still more sagely!

The reason is this: as human nature and the Way exist in the world, without sages and worthies, how could their source be deepened? Without the Song Confucians, there would be no means of channeling their flow. After the teachings of these scholars appeared, gentlemen of later generations could use textual investigation to reject plausible falsehoods, and peer through the gateway to draw out the threadlike strands [?]. Those who fail to see the whole and instead pick faults in one or two particulars are like people bewildered by the waves who forget their source.

I have considered this in the case of Yao. Shun appointed officials; Yu controlled the waters; Ji supervised agriculture; Xie spread instruction; Gao Yao clarified punishments; Bo Kui [?] directed music; and the officials overseeing the regions each discharged their duties. Yao sat above them with folded hands, and the myriad states were thus harmonious. When praising Yao as ruler, people said, “Great indeed!” This was because Yao employed them all according to their talents…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
也又甞觀之天矣日以暄之雨以潤之風
以鼓之雷以動之四時五官之吏各司其
能天無思無爲而萬物自生及言天之道
曰大哉以天包含而徧覆之也蓋觀乎天
又觀乎堯而
成祖暨我
皇上之所以益聖從可知也况乎
聖學心法虞廷之授受也
文華寶鑑夏禹之典則也須經書大全詩之
===
譽髦多士也修爲善陰騭書之康乂兆民
也
鴻謨駿烈孰非自六經中來耶我
皇上明倫大典揭綱常之懿
欽天記頌發昭事之忱
重華有詠闡精一之微
聖學有詩述大學之要
奎章
宸翰又孰非自六經中來耶然要而言之道契
punctuated: 也。又甞觀之天矣：日以暄之，雨以潤之，風以鼓之，雷以動之，四時五官之吏各司其能。天無思無爲，而萬物自生。及言天之道，曰：「大哉！」以天包含而徧覆之也。蓋觀乎天，又觀乎堯，而成祖暨我皇上之所以益聖，從可知也。况乎《聖學心法》，虞廷之授受也；《文華寶鑑》，夏禹之典則也；須《經書大全》，《詩》之「譽髦多士」也；修《爲善陰騭》，《書》之「康乂兆民」也。鴻謨駿烈，孰非自六經中來耶？我皇上《明倫大典》，揭綱常之懿；《欽天記頌》，發昭事之忱；重華有詠，闡精一之微；聖學有詩，述《大學》之要。奎章宸翰，又孰非自六經中來耶？然要而言之，道契
translation_en:
…because he employed men of talent together, each according to his abilities. I have also observed Heaven: the sun warms things, rain moistens them, wind stirs them, and thunder sets them in motion. The officials of the four seasons and the five offices each exercise their abilities. Heaven neither thinks nor acts, yet the myriad things come into being of themselves. When speaking of Heaven’s Way, one says, “How great!” This is because Heaven embraces everything and shelters all beneath it. By observing Heaven and also observing Yao, we can understand how Chengzu and our present Emperor have attained ever greater sageliness.

Moreover, Essentials of the Mind in Sagely Learning (Shengxue xinfa) embodies what was transmitted and received at the court of Shun; the Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian) embodies the models and standards of Yu of the Xia. The passage concerning the Complete Compendia of the Canonical Books (Jingshu daquan) has an unclear verb [?]; it exemplifies the Odes’ “praising the many outstanding men.” Compiling Doing Good and Hidden Recompense (Weishan yinzhi) exemplifies the Documents’ “bringing peace and good government to the multitudes.” Which of these grand plans and mighty achievements did not come from the Six Classics?

Our Emperor’s Great Compendium on Clarifying Human Relations (Minglun dadian) displays the excellence of the cardinal bonds and constant virtues. His Records and Eulogies on Revering Heaven (Qintian jisong) expresses his sincerity in reverently serving Heaven. His verses on Chonghua elucidate the subtle meaning of refinement and single-mindedness; his poems on sagely learning set forth the essentials of the Great Learning. Which of these resplendent compositions, these writings from the imperial brush, did not likewise come from the Six Classics? Yet, to state the essentials, the Way accords with…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
千古
聖人之神也學該諸儒
聖人之量也於此有要焉敬是已惟敬則虛虛
則兼人物通古今會此性之全體而不遺
惟敬則明明則悟道體觀大旨察此性之
淵源而不昧周子所謂主靜立極張子所
謂存心養性爲匪懈程子所謂涵養須用
敬皆所以發明乎是道也蓋至於是然後
知我
===
皇上祖述二帝三王之道光昭
二祖
列聖之學煥四海而垂萬世巍巍乎莫可尚已
愚生沐浴
化育之深誠猶繪天地者難爲工何能揄揚
其盛惟執事進而教之
第二問
鄭淮
考試官教諭陳　批　造理之見該博之學步驟
punctuated:
千古，聖人之神也；學該諸儒，聖人之量也。於此有要焉，敬是已。惟敬則虛，虛則兼人物、通古今，會此性之全體而不遺；惟敬則明，明則悟道體、觀大旨，察此性之淵源而不昧。周子所謂主靜立極，張子所謂存心養性爲匪懈，程子所謂涵養須用敬，皆所以發明乎是道也。蓋至於是，然後知我皇上祖述二帝三王之道，光昭二祖列聖之學，煥四海而垂萬世，巍巍乎莫可尚已。愚生沐浴化育之深，誠猶繪天地者難爲工，何能揄揚其盛？惟執事進而教之。
第二問
鄭淮
考試官教諭陳　批：造理之見，該博之學，步驟
translation_en:
…through the ages—such is the sage’s spiritual power; learning that encompasses all the Confucian scholars—such is the sage’s capacity. There is an essential principle here: reverent attentiveness. Only through reverent attentiveness does one become receptive; through receptivity one embraces people and things, comprehends past and present, and apprehends this nature in its entirety, omitting nothing. Only through reverent attentiveness does one attain clarity; through clarity one understands the substance of the Way, perceives its broad purport, and discerns the deepest sources of this nature without obscurity. Master Zhou’s teaching of making stillness the guiding principle and establishing the ultimate standard, Master Zhang’s teaching of preserving the mind and nourishing one’s nature without flagging, and Master Cheng’s teaching that self-cultivation requires reverent attentiveness all elucidate this Way. Only upon reaching this point does one understand how our Emperor carries forward the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings and gloriously manifests the learning of the Two Founding Emperors and the succession of sage sovereigns, illuminating all within the Four Seas and transmitting it to ten thousand generations. How lofty, beyond all surpassing!
This humble student has been deeply immersed in your transforming instruction and nurture. Yet, just as one who paints Heaven and Earth finds it difficult to do them justice, how could I adequately extol its magnificence? I ask only that you, honored examiners, advance me through your instruction.
Second Question
Zheng Huai
Comment by Examiner Chen, an Instructor: Insights that penetrate principle, learning of comprehensive breadth, a measured progression…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之才正大之論讀之爲子敬容矣
考試官教諭陳　批　論諸家與聖人始同流異
誠非臆說是能尚友而將有得者
夫學者傳蒐載籍權衡往哲必攷其平生
大較與其論著可述於後者鑿鑿有當於
衷設以吾身處其地而安也設起其人于
旣往評騭之而服也而後爲公是公非矣
若不究其操心之實而妄置喙不窺其制
作之閫而遽彈射之是猶借聽於塗之人
===
郢書而燕說之也則謂之何愚甞疑夫老
氏墨氏漢世諸儒皆以一代之英而冒不
韙之譏也且老子嫉世之攘奪於智力非
至人之養身故著道德以諷諭之觀其所
謂知止不殆卽益之謙受益也所謂其政
悶悶卽舜之恭己無爲也所謂天地得一
以清寧卽易之大哉乾元至哉坤元也至
其再傳而蓋公授曹參以成相業豈專以
頤眞也又再傳而河上公授漢文以成帝
punctuated:
之才，正大之論，讀之爲子敬容矣。

考試官教諭陳，批：「論諸家與聖人始同流異，誠非臆說，是能尚友而將有得者。」

夫學者傳蒐載籍，權衡往哲，必攷其平生大較，與其論著可述於後者，鑿鑿有當於衷。設以吾身處其地而安也，設起其人于旣往，評騭之而服也，而後爲公是公非矣。若不究其操心之實而妄置喙，不窺其制作之閫而遽彈射之，是猶借聽於塗之人，郢書而燕說之也，則謂之何？愚甞疑夫老氏、墨氏、漢世諸儒，皆以一代之英而冒不韙之譏也。且老子嫉世之攘奪於智力，非至人之養身，故著《道德》以諷諭之。觀其所謂「知止不殆」，卽《益》之「謙受益」也；所謂「其政悶悶」，卽舜之「恭己無爲」也；所謂「天地得一以清寧」，卽《易》之「大哉乾元，至哉坤元」也。至其再傳，而蓋公授曹參以成相業，豈專以頤眞也？又再傳，而河上公授漢文以成帝
translation_en:
…talent, and upright, broad-minded argument: reading it, I assume an expression of respect for you [?].

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Your argument that the various masters and the sages shared a common starting point but diverged in their subsequent courses is certainly no conjecture. Here is someone capable of befriending the ancients through study and likely to gain understanding.”

When scholars search through the written records [?] and weigh the philosophers of the past, they must investigate the broad outlines of their lives and those writings of theirs worthy of transmission to posterity, reaching conclusions firmly grounded in sound judgment. If I imagine myself in their circumstances, I must find their conduct acceptable; if I imagine bringing them back from the past, my assessment must convince them. Only then can judgments of right and wrong be impartial. To venture opinions without examining the true intentions guiding their minds, or hastily to attack their writings without entering into their inner meaning, is like relying on what one hears from a passerby, or interpreting a letter from Ying in the manner of the man of Yan. What are we to call this? I have long wondered why Laozi, Mozi, and the Confucian scholars of the Han, each outstanding in his age, nevertheless incurred accusations of wrongdoing.

Laozi detested the world’s use of cunning and force to seize things from others, which was contrary to the perfected person’s cultivation of himself. He therefore wrote the Classic of the Way and Virtue to admonish people indirectly. Consider his saying, “Know when to stop, and you will not be imperiled”: this is precisely “Humility receives benefit” in “Benefit” [?]. His saying, “When government is unobtrusive,” is precisely Shun’s “reverently maintaining himself and governing without action.” His saying, “Heaven and earth attain the One and thereby become clear and tranquil,” is precisely what the Book of Changes expresses as “Great indeed is the originating power of Qian! Supreme indeed is the originating power of Kun!” When his teaching had been transmitted a further two times, Master Gai taught Cao Can, enabling him to achieve distinction as Chancellor. Could it have been solely concerned with nourishing one’s authentic nature? After another two transmissions, Heshang Gong taught Emperor Wen of Han, enabling him to accomplish his imperial…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
業豈專以存神也故孔子謂老子其猶龍
也墨子悲世之私便其身圖非仁人之用
心故率天下而盡愛之觀其所謂尚同即
孔之居是邦不非其大夫也所謂兼愛即
孔之汎愛衆博施濟衆爲仁也所謂尚賢
明鬼即孔之好賢如緇衣我祭則受福也
至其里名朝歌爲之回車守已之節非同
流合汙也工於守城敵不知攻濟世之才
非空言無當也故韓愈謂孔子必用墨子
===
不相用不足爲孔墨也然豈惟老氏莊生
俯視宇宙眇小塵寰何其達也胷次之高
殆列禦寇關尹子之流乎豈惟墨氏楊朱
獨潔其身簡易不煩何其介也廉靜之操
其荷蕢接輿之徒乎是數子者制行不同
其必欲爲善之念真切無僞與聖人之心
一也特其爲教或傷於矯枉或病於過高
其流之弊不能無少差殊視中正之道或
以爲有異爾豈薰蕕懸絶也若漢儒傳詩
punctuated:
業，豈專以存神也？故孔子謂老子：「其猶龍也。」墨子悲世之私便其身圖，非仁人之用心，故率天下而盡愛之。觀其所謂尚同，即孔之「居是邦，不非其大夫」也；所謂兼愛，即孔之「汎愛衆」、「博施濟衆爲仁」也；所謂尚賢明鬼，即孔之「好賢如緇衣」、「我祭則受福」也。至其里名朝歌，爲之回車，守已之節，非同流合汙也；工於守城，敵不知攻，濟世之才，非空言無當也。故韓愈謂：「孔子必用墨子，不相用，不足爲孔墨也。」
然豈惟老氏？莊生俯視宇宙，眇小塵寰，何其達也！胷次之高，殆列禦寇、關尹子之流乎？豈惟墨氏？楊朱獨潔其身，簡易不煩，何其介也！廉靜之操，其荷蕢、接輿之徒乎？是數子者，制行不同，其必欲爲善之念，真切無僞，與聖人之心一也。特其爲教，或傷於矯枉，或病於過高，其流之弊，不能無少差殊，視中正之道，或以爲有異爾，豈薰蕕懸絶也？若漢儒傳《詩》
translation_en:
…imperial achievement: was this solely a matter of preserving the spirit? Thus Confucius said of Laozi, “He is like a dragon.” Mozi lamented that people selfishly sought their own advantage [?], which was not how a humane person set his mind; he therefore led all under Heaven toward loving everyone. Consider his doctrine of “exalting conformity”: it corresponds to Confucius’s saying, “When residing in a state, do not disparage its great officers.” His “impartial care” corresponds to Confucius’s “love the multitude broadly” and “widely bestowing benefits and aiding the multitude constitutes humaneness.” His “exalting the worthy” and “elucidating spirits” correspond to Confucius’s “loving the worthy as in ‘Black Robes’” and “when I offer sacrifice, I receive blessings.” When he encountered a settlement named Chaoge, “Morning Song,” he turned his carriage back: this was integrity in maintaining his own standards, not drifting with the current and joining in corruption. He was so skilled in defending cities that enemies did not know how to attack them: this was talent for helping the world, not empty, impractical talk. Thus Han Yu said, “Confucius would surely have employed Mozi. Had they not employed one another, they would not have been worthy of being Confucius and Mozi.”
Yet why speak only of Laozi? Master Zhuang looked down upon the cosmos and regarded the dusty mortal world as insignificant. How broad his understanding! In loftiness of mind, was he not perhaps of the same company as Lie Yukou and Guanyinzi? Why speak only of Mozi? Yang Zhu alone kept himself pure, living simply and without complication. How firm his integrity! In his incorruptible and tranquil conduct, was he not of the company of the basket-bearer and Jieyu? These masters differed in how they regulated their conduct, but their determination to do good was sincere and free of pretence, one with the mind of the sage. It was only that their teachings sometimes suffered from overcorrection or from setting their sights too high. The faults of their later schools could not be entirely free of slight deviations; measured against the way of centrality and rectitude, they might therefore be considered somewhat different. But were they as utterly opposed as fragrant and foul-smelling plants? As for the Han scholars who transmitted the Book of Odes…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
書與易者各四家傳禮與春秋者各三家
是數家者或子孫相繩守其世業或生徒
傳受守其師說購求於秦灰之餘論次於
殘缺之後良工用心亦已勤矣故太史公
列諸儒林也由今而觀董子之醇正賈生
之通達申公之持重夏侯勝之力學鄭康
成之博洽匡衡之經濟京房之占候孔安
國之注疏伏生之强識劉子駿之著作皆
卓然爲當時之名家六籍之羽翼也蓋兩
===
漢去古未遠其心習渾厚非涼德薄識者
之可倫其經學專門非掇拾糟粕者之可
比假使當時無漢之諸儒則祖龍以降學
之傳於今者刑名之習卜筮種樹之說爾
宋儒雖有表章之功亦何所考據以取衷
也世之人乃謂其不學無術此何異渡江
河而忘其楫悅虎豹之文而去其皮也然
漢人之可傳者獨經術已哉語史學司馬
氏史記良史之宗也語詩學蘇李故乘古
punctuated: 書與易者各四家，傳禮與春秋者各三家。是數家者，或子孫相繩，守其世業；或生徒傳受，守其師說。購求於秦灰之餘，論次於殘缺之後，良工用心，亦已勤矣。故太史公列諸儒林也。由今而觀，董子之醇正，賈生之通達，申公之持重，夏侯勝之力學，鄭康成之博洽，匡衡之經濟，京房之占候，孔安國之注疏，伏生之强識，劉子駿之著作，皆卓然爲當時之名家、六籍之羽翼也。蓋兩漢去古未遠，其心習渾厚，非涼德薄識者之可倫；其經學專門，非掇拾糟粕者之可比。假使當時無漢之諸儒，則祖龍以降，學之傳於今者，刑名之習、卜筮種樹之說爾。宋儒雖有表章之功，亦何所考據以取衷也？世之人乃謂其不學無術，此何異渡江河而忘其楫，悅虎豹之文而去其皮也？然漢人之可傳者，獨經術已哉？語史學，司馬氏《史記》，良史之宗也；語詩學，蘇李故乘古
translation_en:
…the Documents and the Changes each had four schools of transmission, while the Rites and the Spring and Autumn Annals each had three. Among these schools, some were maintained by descendants who continued their families’ scholarly work; others were transmitted among pupils who preserved their teachers’ interpretations. They sought out and purchased what survived the ashes of Qin, arranging and discussing the texts after their mutilation and loss. These skilled workers certainly devoted painstaking effort to their task. Thus the Grand Astrologer included them in his account of the Confucian scholars.

Viewed from the present, Master Dong’s purity and rectitude, Master Jia’s breadth of understanding, Master Shen’s sober judgment, Xiahou Sheng’s diligence in study, Zheng Kangcheng’s extensive learning, Kuang Heng’s ability in statecraft, Jing Fang’s prognostication, Kong Anguo’s commentaries, Master Fu’s powerful memory, and Liu Zijun’s writings all made them outstanding authorities in their own day and supports for the Six Classics. The two Han dynasties were, after all, not far removed from antiquity. Their scholars’ dispositions and habits were substantial and sincere, beyond comparison with those of scant virtue and shallow understanding. Their specialized mastery of the classics could not be matched by those who merely picked up the dregs of learning.

Had there been no such Confucian scholars under the Han, the learning transmitted to our own day from the time of Zulong—the First Emperor of Qin—onward would have consisted merely of the study of punishments and administrative accountability, and teachings on divination and tree planting. Even though the Song Confucians did much to elucidate and promote the classics, what evidence would they have had to examine in order to arrive at sound judgments? Yet people now call the Han scholars unlearned and devoid of method. How is this different from crossing a river and forgetting one’s oars, or admiring the markings of tigers and leopards while discarding their hides?

But was classical learning the only Han achievement worthy of transmission? In historical scholarship, Sima’s Records of the Historian is the exemplar of good history; in poetry, the old writings of Su Wu and Li Ling [?], in the ancient…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
風之祖也語政事龔黃韓趙吏治蓋烝烝
焉語詞賦相如子雲文學蓋彬彬焉語邊
功衛霍在西北虜庭至今稱漢也語奉使
陸賈張騫在西南荒徼至今歸一統也試
使後世論議之儒與漢材比氣量力較藝
程能豈可得同日語哉大抵論人於三代
之下老莊楊墨一世之高士也漢代諸儒
百世之豪士也諄諄者不察其心毛比繩
引其蔽豈直無星之稱無寸之尺已哉
===
第三問
同考試官教諭黃 批兵法兵制士子類能言之
此篇條達詳明宜錄以式
考試官教諭陳 批蓋嘗究心武備者
考試官教諭陳 批典雅敷暢
制天下以威故治世不可以去兵也馭天
下以勢故盛世不可以忘備也蓋天下之
患常隱於未形而幾每兆於未著患未形
punctuated:
風之祖也。語政事，龔、黃、韓、趙，吏治蓋烝烝焉；語詞賦，相如、子雲，文學蓋彬彬焉；語邊功，衛、霍在西北，虜庭至今稱漢也；語奉使，陸賈、張騫在西南，荒徼至今歸一統也。試使後世論議之儒與漢材比氣量力、較藝程能，豈可得同日語哉？大抵論人於三代之下，老、莊、楊、墨，一世之高士也；漢代諸儒，百世之豪士也。諄諄者不察其心，毛比繩引，其蔽豈直無星之稱、無寸之尺已哉？

第三問

同考試官教諭黃批：兵法兵制，士子類能言之，此篇條達詳明，宜錄以式。

考試官教諭陳批：蓋嘗究心武備者。

考試官教諭陳批：典雅敷暢。

制天下以威，故治世不可以去兵也；馭天下以勢，故盛世不可以忘備也。蓋天下之患常隱於未形，而幾每兆於未著。患未形
translation_en:
…the progenitors of the ancient poetic style. In government, Gong, Huang, Han, and Zhao brought flourishing achievements in local administration. In verse and rhapsody, Xiangru and Ziyun displayed splendid literary refinement. In frontier exploits, Wei and Huo campaigned in the northwest, where the courts of the foreign peoples still speak of the Han today. In diplomatic service, Lu Jia and Zhang Qian operated in the southwest, whose remote borderlands remain within a unified realm to this day. Suppose the argumentative scholars of later ages were measured against the talented men of the Han in spirit and strength, and compared in accomplishment and ability: how could they possibly be spoken of in the same breath? Broadly speaking, among men since the Three Dynasties, Laozi, Zhuangzi, Yang Zhu, and Mozi were lofty scholars of a single age; the Confucian scholars of the Han were outstanding men for a hundred generations. Those who endlessly argue fail to examine their intentions, making hair-splitting comparisons and judging them by rigid measures [?]. Is their blindness merely that of a balance without graduations or a ruler without inch marks?

Third Question

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: “Candidates can generally discuss military methods and military institutions. This essay is orderly, thorough, and clear; it should be recorded as a model.”

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “The author evidently has devoted serious attention to military preparedness.”

Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “Classically elegant, expansive, and fluent.”

All under Heaven is controlled through awe-inspiring might; therefore, even in an age of good government, arms cannot be dispensed with. All under Heaven is governed through strategic advantage; therefore, even in a flourishing age, preparedness must not be forgotten. For the troubles of the realm commonly lie hidden before taking shape, and incipient developments often give signs before becoming apparent. When troubles have not yet taken shape…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
則人心狃於故常所以威天下之具不能
不病於因循幾未著則人心忽於隱微所
以固根本之地不能不敝於玩愒則吾之
所以鞭撻四夷蕩平草竊者舛其機所以
慎固根本居重馭輕者違其道是豈可不
講之於素而備之於豫乎故易曰弧矢之
利以威天下又曰重門擊柝以待暴客誠
聖王之所不廢盛世之所當務也執事發
策以兵法兵制下詢承學書生談兵昔人
===
恥之然載在典籍竊嘗玫識萬一敢掇拾
以答明問可乎何謂兵法黃帝象五行以
制五陣曰金木水火土所謂五行陣也太
公效三才以制三陣曰天地人所謂三才
陣也風氏始創八陣則有天地風雲龍虎
鳥蛇者是也孫臏嘗制八陣則有方圓牝
牡衝方罘罝車輪鴈行者是也吳起爲戰
國名將固不能舍陣法以爲戰乃又爲曲
直銳卦車箱車釭鵞鶴衝陣蓋亦因風氏
punctuated:
則人心狃於故常，所以威天下之具不能不病於因循；幾未著，則人心忽於隱微，所以固根本之地不能不敝於玩愒。則吾之所以鞭撻四夷、蕩平草竊者舛其機，所以慎固根本、居重馭輕者違其道。是豈可不講之於素而備之於豫乎？故《易》曰：「弧矢之利，以威天下。」又曰：「重門擊柝，以待暴客。」誠聖王之所不廢，盛世之所當務也。執事發策，以兵法兵制下詢承學。書生談兵，昔人恥之；然載在典籍，竊嘗玫識萬一，敢掇拾以答明問，可乎？

何謂兵法？黃帝象五行以制五陣，曰金、木、水、火、土，所謂五行陣也。太公效三才以制三陣，曰天、地、人，所謂三才陣也。風氏始創八陣，則有天地風雲龍虎鳥蛇者是也。孫臏嘗制八陣，則有方、圓、牝、牡、衝方、罘罝、車輪、鴈行者是也。吳起爲戰國名將，固不能舍陣法以爲戰，乃又爲曲、直、銳、卦、車箱、車釭、鵞鶴、衝陣，蓋亦因風氏
translation_en:
…then people become habituated to established ways, and the means of overawing all under Heaven inevitably suffer from unthinking adherence to precedent. When the first signs have not yet become apparent, people neglect what is hidden and subtle, and the places that secure the foundations inevitably deteriorate through complacency and delay. Thus our means of chastising the peoples of the four quarters and suppressing petty bandits go awry in their operation, while our means of carefully securing the foundations and controlling the lesser from the center of power depart from their proper course. How, then, could these matters fail to require regular study and advance preparation? Hence the Book of Changes says: “The advantage of bows and arrows serves to overawe all under Heaven.” It also says: “Double gates and the striking of watch-clappers serve to await violent intruders.” These are indeed things that sage kings never dispense with and that flourishing ages ought to attend to. Your Honor has issued a policy question concerning military methods and institutions, graciously consulting us students. For a scholar to discuss warfare was something men of old considered shameful. Yet these matters are recorded in the canonical writings, and I have privately tried to learn a tiny portion of them [?]. May I venture to gather what I know in reply to your discerning question?

What are military methods? The Yellow Emperor modeled five formations on the Five Phases: metal, wood, water, fire, and earth. These are the so-called Five Phases formations. The Grand Duke modeled three formations on the Three Powers: Heaven, Earth, and humanity. These are the so-called Three Powers formations. Fengshi first devised eight formations: heaven, earth, wind, cloud, dragon, tiger, bird, and snake. Sun Bin devised eight formations: square, round, female, male, assault-square, net, chariot-wheel, and wild-goose-file. Wu Qi, a renowned general of the Warring States period, certainly could not wage war without methods of deployment. He further devised the curved, straight, pointed, trigram [?], chariot-box, chariot-hub, goose-and-crane, and assault formations. These, too, presumably followed Fengshi’s…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之制而興其名耳武侯爲三國將相亦不
能外陣法以用兵乃又爲洞當中黃龍騰
鳥翔連衡握奇虎翼折衝蓋亦因吳起之
法而師其意耳至於有唐李靖爲一代名
將武功莫尚焉靖則以八陣人皆習聞而
知之不可不移敵人之耳目於是又變爲
六花陣焉中軍之外爲左右虞候左右四
廂之六名又爲十二陣焉中軍之外爲遊
奕大黑大赤當子午青蛇白虎當卯酉爲
===
四正左突右擊當寅申前衝後衝當巳亥
摧鋒決勝當辰戌破敵先鋒當丑未爲四
奇蓋按月將日躔而用之者也遡求夫周
禮大司馬九伐之法曰眚曰伐曰壇曰削
曰侵曰正曰殘曰杜曰滅所謂正正之師
不可尚矣下迨夫孫子九地之術曰散地
曰輕地曰爭地曰交地曰衢地曰重地曰
險地曰危地曰絕地所謂善善之道亦云
至矣鼂錯人稱爲智囊其立言有謂五技
punctuated: 之制而興其名耳。武侯爲三國將相，亦不能外陣法以用兵，乃又爲洞當、中黃、龍騰、鳥翔、連衡、握奇、虎翼、折衝，蓋亦因吳起之法而師其意耳。至於有唐，李靖爲一代名將，武功莫尚焉。靖則以八陣人皆習聞而知之，不可不移敵人之耳目，於是又變爲六花陣焉。中軍之外，爲左右虞候、左右四廂之六名。又爲十二陣焉，中軍之外，爲遊奕。大黑、大赤當子午，青蛇、白虎當卯酉，爲四正；左突、右擊當寅申，前衝、後衝當巳亥，摧鋒、決勝當辰戌，破敵、先鋒當丑未，爲四奇。蓋按月將日躔而用之者也。遡求夫《周禮》大司馬九伐之法，曰眚、曰伐、曰壇、曰削、曰侵、曰正、曰殘、曰杜、曰滅，所謂正正之師，不可尚矣。下迨夫《孫子》九地之術，曰散地、曰輕地、曰爭地、曰交地、曰衢地、曰重地、曰險地、曰危地、曰絕地，所謂善善之道，亦云至矣。鼂錯，人稱爲智囊，其立言有謂五技
translation_en:
…merely following his system and introducing these names. The Martial Marquis, a general and chief minister in the Three Kingdoms period, likewise could not conduct warfare apart from formation methods. He therefore devised Dongdang (Cave-front [?]), Zhonghuang (Central Yellow), Longteng (Soaring Dragon), Niaoxiang (Flying Bird), Lianheng (Linked Lines), Woqi (Holding the Extraordinary), Huyi (Tiger’s Wings), and Zhechong (Breaking the Assault). These too followed Wu Qi’s methods and took their underlying principles as a model.

In the Tang dynasty, Li Jing was an outstanding general of his age, unsurpassed in military achievements. Jing considered that everyone was familiar with the Eight Formations, having often heard of them, and that it was therefore necessary to confuse the enemy’s eyes and ears. He accordingly transformed them into the Six Flowers Formation. Apart from the central army, its six divisions were the left and right scouting commands and the four wings on the left and right. He also devised twelve formations, with a roving force outside the central army. Great Black and Great Red corresponded to zi and wu; Azure Snake and White Tiger corresponded to mao and you: these constituted the four regular positions. Left Thrust and Right Strike corresponded to yin and shen; Front Charge and Rear Charge to si and hai; Breaking the Spearhead and Securing Victory to chen and xu; Defeating the Enemy and Vanguard to chou and wei: these constituted the four extraordinary positions [?]. Their deployment followed the monthly celestial governors and the sun’s position in the heavens.

Looking further back, the methods of the nine punitive expeditions prescribed for the Minister of War in the Rites of Zhou were called sheng (diminishment), fa (attack), tan (leveling [?]), xue (territorial reduction), qin (incursion), zheng (rectification [?]), can (devastation), du (blockade), and mie (annihilation). These were what is meant by an army in impeccable order: nothing could surpass them. Coming down to the methods for the nine kinds of ground in Master Sun’s Art of War, these were dispersive ground, light ground, contested ground, intersecting ground, thoroughfare ground, heavy ground, difficult ground, perilous ground [?], and cut-off ground [?]. What is called the way of supreme excellence may likewise be said to have reached its utmost here. Chao Cuo, whom people called a “bag of wisdom,” spoke in his writings of five military skills…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
一曰輕車突騎二曰勁弩長戟三曰堅甲
利刃四曰材官騶發五曰下馬地鬬此皆
中國之所長匈奴之所短也孔明自比於
管樂其立訓有謂五習一曰目習識旌旗
之號二曰耳習察金鼓之聲三曰心習精
教令之事四曰手習熟五兵之器五曰足
習譸赴引之利此在我卒有服習之效可
不戰而屈人之兵矣夫用兵所以除殘救
民也黃帝風氏之君相武王太公之君臣
===
所謂仁義之師非後世所能及孔明以正
名而輔漢李靖以戡亂而興唐皆節制紀
律之兵亦庶幾順天應人之舉矣至於孫
吳之徒肆封豕長蛇之毒以魚肉生民者
豈可同日而語哉何謂兵制漢置南北軍
而以八校尉分隷之曰中壘曰屯騎曰步
兵曰越騎曰長水曰胡騎曰射聲曰虎賁
蓋宮城門內之衛也隋定十二衛而以四
將軍分統之曰翊左曰翊右曰驍左曰驍
punctuated:
一曰輕車突騎，二曰勁弩長戟，三曰堅甲利刃，四曰材官騶發，五曰下馬地鬬。此皆中國之所長、匈奴之所短也。孔明自比於管樂，其立訓有謂五習：一曰目習，識旌旗之號；二曰耳習，察金鼓之聲；三曰心習，精教令之事；四曰手習，熟五兵之器；五曰足習，譸赴引之利。此在我卒有服習之效，可不戰而屈人之兵矣。夫用兵，所以除殘救民也。黃帝、風氏之君相，武王、太公之君臣，所謂仁義之師，非後世所能及。孔明以正名而輔漢，李靖以戡亂而興唐，皆節制紀律之兵，亦庶幾順天應人之舉矣。至於孫吳之徒，肆封豕長蛇之毒，以魚肉生民者，豈可同日而語哉？

何謂兵制？漢置南北軍，而以八校尉分隷之：曰中壘，曰屯騎，曰步兵，曰越騎，曰長水，曰胡騎，曰射聲，曰虎賁。蓋宮城門內之衛也。隋定十二衛，而以四將軍分統之：曰翊左，曰翊右，曰驍左，曰驍
translation_en:
…First, light chariots and shock cavalry; second, powerful crossbows and long halberds; third, sturdy armor and sharp blades; fourth, trained infantry firing in volleys [?]; fifth, dismounting to fight on the ground. These are all strengths of the Central Kingdom and weaknesses of the Xiongnu. Kongming compared himself to Guan Zhong and Yue Yi. In his instructions he spoke of five kinds of training: first, training the eyes to recognize the signals of banners and flags; second, training the ears to distinguish the sounds of gongs and drums; third, training the mind to master commands and orders; fourth, training the hands to become proficient with the five kinds of weapons; fifth, training the feet to gain the advantage in advancing and withdrawing [?]. When our soldiers have acquired proficiency through such training, we can subdue the enemy’s forces without fighting.

The purpose of employing troops is to eliminate the cruel and save the people. The Yellow Emperor and Feng, as ruler and minister, and King Wu and the Grand Duke, as sovereign and subject, led what were called armies of benevolence and righteousness, which later generations could not equal. Kongming assisted the Han by upholding its rightful title; Li Jing brought the Tang to ascendancy by quelling disorder. Their armies were all subject to command and discipline, and their undertakings came close to according with Heaven and answering the wishes of the people. As for the likes of Sun Wu and Wu Qi, who unleashed the venom of great boars and long serpents, treating the people as fish and meat to be devoured—how could they be spoken of in the same breath?

What is meant by military organization? The Han established the Southern and Northern Armies, assigning their units to eight commandants: the Commandant of the Central Rampart, the Commandant of Garrison Cavalry, the Commandant of Infantry, the Commandant of Yue Cavalry, the Commandant of Changshui, the Commandant of Hu Cavalry, the Commandant of Archers Who Shoot by Sound, and the Commandant of the Tiger Guards. These were the guards within the gates of the palace city. The Sui established twelve guards, dividing their command among four generals: the Left Supporting Guard, the Right Supporting Guard, the Left Valiant Guard, and the Valiant…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
右曰屯左曰屯右曰武左曰武右曰禦左
曰禦右蓋都會禁兵之法也唐酌隋府兵
之舊而建三衛則以貴戚大臣子弟爲之
曰親衛曰勳衛曰翊衛别置左右羽林龍
武神武之六衛又有左右衛左右驍衛武
衛威衛領軍金吾監門千牛之十二衛焉
唐府兵之法頗爲近古誠一代之善制也
宋因五代侍衛之制而立三衙則以樞密
院掌之曰殿前司曰侍衛馬軍曰侍衛步
===
軍外置捧日天武龍衛神衛之四廂又有
左右金吾大將軍諸衛上將軍諸衛大將
軍諸將軍府率副率之十衛焉宋禁軍之
法頗稱强幹誠一代之良法也夫制兵所
以重內輕外也而掌之之善尤在得人漢
如金日磾之樫符張安世之當軸皆以謹
厚稱宋如王審琦之宿衛石守信之典兵
皆以雄武稱亦庶幾師貞丈人之吉矣若
唐之立法其始也爲最善其終也爲最敝
punctuated:
右，曰屯左，曰屯右，曰武左，曰武右，曰禦左，曰禦右，蓋都會禁兵之法也。唐酌隋府兵之舊而建三衛，則以貴戚大臣子弟爲之，曰親衛，曰勳衛，曰翊衛。别置左右羽林、龍武、神武之六衛，又有左右衛、左右驍衛、武衛、威衛、領軍、金吾、監門、千牛之十二衛焉。唐府兵之法頗爲近古，誠一代之善制也。宋因五代侍衛之制而立三衙，則以樞密院掌之，曰殿前司，曰侍衛馬軍，曰侍衛步軍。外置捧日、天武、龍衛、神衛之四廂，又有左右金吾大將軍、諸衛上將軍、諸衛大將軍、諸將軍、府率、副率之十衛焉。宋禁軍之法頗稱强幹，誠一代之良法也。

夫制兵所以重內輕外也，而掌之之善尤在得人。漢如金日磾之樫符、張安世之當軸，皆以謹厚稱；宋如王審琦之宿衛、石守信之典兵，皆以雄武稱，亦庶幾師貞丈人之吉矣。若唐之立法，其始也爲最善，其終也爲最敝。
translation_en:
…the Right Valiant Guard, the Left Encampment Guard, the Right Encampment Guard, the Left Military Guard, the Right Military Guard, the Left Defense Guard, and the Right Defense Guard: this was the system for the imperial troops in the capital. Drawing on the old Sui system of militia units (fubing), the Tang established three guards, staffed by sons and younger kinsmen of imperial relatives and high officials: the Personal Guard, the Meritorious Guard, and the Escort Guard. Separately, it established six guards—the Left and Right Feathered Forest, Dragon Military, and Divine Military Guards. There were also the twelve guards [?]: the Left and Right Guards, Valiant Guards, Military Guards, Awesome Guards, Army-Leading Guards, Imperial Insignia Guards, Gate Monitoring Guards, and Thousand Oxen Guards. The Tang militia system came quite close to that of antiquity and was truly an excellent institution of its age. Following the Five Dynasties’ system of palace guards, the Song established the Three Commands under the Bureau of Military Affairs: the Palace Command, the Palace Cavalry Command, and the Palace Infantry Command. In addition, it established four divisions: Sun Upholding, Heavenly Military, Dragon Guard, and Divine Guard. There were also ten guards [?], with Left and Right Imperial Insignia Guard Generals-in-chief, Supreme Generals of the various guards, Generals-in-chief of the various guards, generals, guard commandants, and vice commandants. The Song imperial army system was much praised for strengthening the central government and was truly an excellent arrangement of its age.

The purpose of organizing the army is to give greater weight to the center and less to the outlying regions; yet administering it well depends above all on finding the right men. Under the Han, Jin Midi, who held the military tallies [?], and Zhang Anshi, who occupied a pivotal position, were both renowned for their circumspection and integrity. Under the Song, Wang Shenqi, who served in the palace guard, and Shi Shouxin, who commanded troops, were both renowned for their martial prowess. These examples came close to realizing the auspicious outcome described in the Book of Changes: an army steadfast in correctness, led by a mature man. As for the institutions established by the Tang, they were the best at their inception, but the most corrupted by their end.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
府兵變而爲彍騎彍騎變而爲藩鎮其視
漢宋之法不侔矣蓋嘗謂兵不可無法也
而貴於精兵不精則無以威示四夷而震
肅八紘矣然精兵非難任將爲難孫子曰
未戰而廟筭勝者得筭多者也晁錯曰將
不知兵是以主予敵也蓋任將之道必如
莊子所謂驗之以九徵太公所謂稽之以
八徵尤必推之以誠信寄之以心膂推轂
受戍以隆其禮建牙授鉞以重其權如是
===
而威不加於四海者吾不信也兵不可無
制也而貴於戢兵不戢則悍獷之風熾而
綱紀之日弛矣然戢兵非難養兵爲難孔
子曰足食足兵易曰君子以容民畜衆蓋
養兵之道莫善於漢之屯田唐之府兵必
如均土而稽考力而任遞役而征番上而
直如是而勢不固於磐石者吾不信也愚
也蠡管之識迂腐之談不達時務惟執事
進而教之幸莫大焉
punctuated:
府兵變而爲彍騎，彍騎變而爲藩鎮，其視漢宋之法不侔矣。蓋嘗謂兵不可無法也，而貴於精；兵不精，則無以威示四夷而震肅八紘矣。然精兵非難，任將爲難。孫子曰：「未戰而廟筭勝者，得筭多者也。」晁錯曰：「將不知兵，是以主予敵也。」蓋任將之道，必如莊子所謂驗之以九徵，太公所謂稽之以八徵，尤必推之以誠信，寄之以心膂，推轂受戍，以隆其禮；建牙授鉞，以重其權。如是而威不加於四海者，吾不信也。
兵不可無制也，而貴於戢；兵不戢，則悍獷之風熾，而綱紀之日弛矣。然戢兵非難，養兵爲難。孔子曰：「足食足兵。」《易》曰：「君子以容民畜衆。」蓋養兵之道，莫善於漢之屯田、唐之府兵。必如均土而稽，考力而任，遞役而征，番上而直。如是而勢不固於磐石者，吾不信也。愚也，蠡管之識，迂腐之談，不達時務，惟執事進而教之，幸莫大焉。
translation_en:
…The militia system (fubing) changed into the expanded cavalry (guoqi), and the expanded cavalry gave way to the regional military commands (fanzhen). Compared with the systems of the Han and Song, it was no longer their equal. I have long maintained that troops cannot do without rules, but what matters most is their quality. If troops lack quality, there is no way to display might before the peoples of the four quarters and inspire awe throughout the eight expanses of the world. Yet making troops effective is not the difficult thing; appointing generals is. Sunzi said: “Those whose temple calculations indicate victory before battle have obtained many favorable reckonings.” Chao Cuo said: “When a general does not understand warfare, this amounts to handing his ruler over to the enemy.” In appointing generals, one must therefore examine them through the nine tests described by Zhuangzi and assess them through the eight tests described by the Grand Duke (Taigong). Above all, one must extend sincere trust to them and entrust them with responsibilities as one's own heart and sinews. By ceremonially pushing forward their chariot wheels and receiving a garrison commission [?], one magnifies the honors accorded them; by erecting their command standards and bestowing the battle-axe, one enhances their authority. I cannot believe that, with such measures, one's might would fail to extend throughout the Four Seas.
Troops cannot do without regulation, but what matters most is restraint. If troops are not restrained, a fierce and unruly spirit flourishes, while discipline grows laxer by the day. Yet restraining troops is not the difficult thing; sustaining them is. Confucius said: “Sufficient food and sufficient troops.” The Book of Changes says: “The gentleman thereby accommodates the people and nourishes the multitude.” For sustaining troops, nothing surpasses the military agricultural colonies of the Han and the militia system of the Tang. One must distribute land equitably and conduct inspections, assess men's strength and assign responsibilities, levy them for service in rotation, and have them report for duty in alternating turns. I cannot believe that, with such measures, one's position would fail to be as firm as a great rock. My understanding is narrow, like measuring with a ladle or viewing through a tube; my discourse is pedantic, and I fail to comprehend the affairs of the day. If you, honored examiners, would receive me and instruct me, no greater good fortune could be mine.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
第四問
饒養浩
同考試官教諭梁　批　荒政區畫切中時宜且能
揄揚
聖上以和召和之徵子其抱文正之志者乎錄之
考試官教諭陳　批　知重民命通達治體
考試官教諭陳　批　酌古準今之學
爲治者當酌諸古而泥於文者失之君子
以爲師其意可也亦當通乎今而徇於俗
===
者失之君子以爲達夫權可也夫意也者
其先王經綸之運乎權也者其用世應變
之機乎泥古之文而不師其意則無以知
創制立法之善其失也拘徇今之俗而不
達其權則無以得隨宜救弊之方其失也
謬書曰監于先王成憲其永無愆其稽古
之則也易曰通其變使民不倦其通今之
準也執事以荒政下詢承學蓋以識時務
者望之也愚非其人也嘗竊窺聖人爲民
punctuated:
第四問

饒養浩

同考試官教諭梁批：荒政區畫，切中時宜，且能揄揚聖上以和召和之徵。子其抱文正之志者乎？錄之。

考試官教諭陳批：知重民命，通達治體。

考試官教諭陳批：酌古準今之學。

爲治者當酌諸古，而泥於文者失之。君子以爲師其意可也。亦當通乎今，而徇於俗者失之。君子以爲達夫權可也。夫意也者，其先王經綸之運乎？權也者，其用世應變之機乎？泥古之文而不師其意，則無以知創制立法之善，其失也拘；徇今之俗而不達其權，則無以得隨宜救弊之方，其失也謬。《書》曰：「監于先王成憲，其永無愆。」其稽古之則也。《易》曰：「通其變，使民不倦。」其通今之準也。執事以荒政下詢承學，蓋以識時務者望之也。愚非其人也，嘗竊窺聖人爲民
translation_en:
Fourth Policy Question

Rao Yanghao

Comment by Associate Examiner Liang, Instructor: “The planning of famine relief precisely meets present needs. Moreover, he ably praises the evidence that His Majesty’s harmony calls forth harmony. Might you be one who cherishes the aspirations of Lord Wenzheng? Accept this essay.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “He understands the importance of the people’s lives and thoroughly comprehends the essentials of governance.”

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor: “Learning that weighs antiquity against the circumstances of the present.”

Those who govern should weigh the precedents of antiquity, but those who cling to their outward forms go astray. The gentleman considers it proper to take their underlying intent as one’s guide. One should also understand the present, but those who merely follow prevailing customs go astray. The gentleman considers it proper to comprehend how to exercise discretion. Is not this underlying intent the guiding purpose by which the former kings ordered the world? Is not discretion the means of engaging with the world and responding to change? If one clings to the outward forms of antiquity without taking their intent as one’s guide, one cannot understand what made the establishment of institutions and laws beneficial: the resulting error is rigidity. If one follows present customs without understanding how to exercise discretion, one cannot find ways to remedy abuses as circumstances require: the resulting error is misjudgment. The Book of Documents says: “Look to the established statutes of the former kings, and you will forever be free from error.” This is the rule for examining antiquity. The Book of Changes says: “Adapt to changes, so that the people do not grow weary.” This is the standard for understanding the present.

You, sir, have condescended to question us students about famine relief, evidently expecting us to understand the needs of the times. Unworthy as I am, I am not such a person. Yet I have ventured to glimpse the sages’ concern for the people …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
無已之心矣其慮天下也甚周故患未生
而豫爲之備其救天下也甚詳故害旣至
而曲爲之防其視天下也眞猶吾之一體
有一民一物之不得其所誠若痌瘝疾痛
之切於其身者豈但已耶蓋觀於周禮而
知之矣如井田之法監於黃帝夏商之規
而損益之鄉遂用貢法曰遂曰溝曰洫曰
川則遂人所掌焉都鄙用助法曰井曰邑
曰丘曰甸曰縣則匠人所掌焉其於財用
===
所以生之者有道矣三年耕餘一年之食
九年耕餘三年之食以三十年之通制國
用量入以爲出所以積之者有素矣夫生
之有道積之有素則旣備之未患矣故雖
有災歉之値亦將恃以無恐若是足矣而
又有十二荒政豈聖人之過計哉災祥間
出世代有之聖人不能必變之不生而恃
吾有濟之之術堯有九年之水湯有七年
之旱而國無捐瘠者凡以備之有素而救
punctuated: 無已之心矣。其慮天下也甚周，故患未生而豫爲之備；其救天下也甚詳，故害旣至而曲爲之防。其視天下也，眞猶吾之一體，有一民一物之不得其所，誠若痌瘝疾痛之切於其身者，豈但已耶？蓋觀於《周禮》而知之矣。如井田之法，監於黃帝夏商之規而損益之。鄉遂用貢法，曰遂、曰溝、曰洫、曰川，則遂人所掌焉；都鄙用助法，曰井、曰邑、曰丘、曰甸、曰縣，則匠人所掌焉。其於財用，所以生之者有道矣。三年耕，餘一年之食；九年耕，餘三年之食。以三十年之通制國用，量入以爲出，所以積之者有素矣。夫生之有道，積之有素，則旣備之未患矣。故雖有災歉之値，亦將恃以無恐。若是足矣，而又有十二荒政，豈聖人之過計哉？災祥間出，世代有之。聖人不能必變之不生，而恃吾有濟之之術。堯有九年之水，湯有七年之旱，而國無捐瘠者，凡以備之有素而救
translation_en:
…their unceasing concern for the people. The sages’ care for all under Heaven was exceedingly comprehensive; thus, before troubles arose, they prepared against them. Their measures to save all under Heaven were exceedingly thorough; thus, once harm had arrived, they guarded against it in every particular. They truly regarded all under Heaven as their own body. If even one person or one creature failed to find its proper place, they felt it as keenly as suffering and illness in their own bodies. How could they simply stop at that? We can understand this by examining the Rites of Zhou.

Take the well-field system: they looked to the arrangements of the Yellow Emperor and the Xia and Shang dynasties, modifying them through subtraction and addition. The districts and outlying districts employed the tribute method. The channels called sui [?], gou, xu, and chuan were under the charge of the Director of Outlying Districts. The domains and estates employed the labor-assistance method. The units called jing, yi, qiu, dian, and xian were under the charge of the Master Craftsman. Thus, they had sound methods for generating fiscal resources. Three years of cultivation yielded a surplus sufficient for one year’s food; nine years of cultivation yielded a surplus sufficient for three years’ food. State expenditure was regulated on the basis of an aggregate reckoning over thirty years, with outlays determined by revenue. Thus, they had established arrangements for accumulating reserves.

With sound methods of production and established arrangements for accumulation, provision was already made against troubles before they arose [?]. Consequently, even when disasters and poor harvests occurred, these reserves could be relied upon to dispel fear. Such measures would seem sufficient, yet there were also twelve measures for famine relief. Was this excessive planning on the sages’ part? Calamities and auspicious events occur in alternation; every age has them. The sages could not ensure that disruptions would never arise, but relied on possessing the means to bring people through them. Yao endured nine years of flooding, and Tang seven years of drought, yet within their realms none were abandoned to starvation. This was entirely because their preparations were long established and their relief …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之有方也故適然之數不能傷如天之仁
虧允殖之治以是知處堯湯之後荒政尤
不可已也試以周禮荒政言之散利之外
其曰薄征以蘇其財也曰弛役以寛其力
也乃用之以濟荒不可緩也曰緩刑以全
其生也曰蕃樂以節其情也曰殺盜以除
其害也乃資之以治荒不可廢也若夫舍
禁去譏卽傳之所謂通商惠工而非以爲
縱也眚禮殺哀卽易之所謂損益盈虛而
===
非以爲簡也其索鬼也卽詩之所謂靡神
不舉而非以爲誣也其多昏也卽易之所
謂愆期有待而非以爲瀆也于斯見聖人
敬天之實焉于斯見聖人勤民之政焉周
禮一書誠周公致太平之書萬世治天下
者之準則也降及後世履畝稅於魯阡陌
開於秦而井田之法壞雖代有限田均田
口分世業之制亦不過剜肉補瘡之爲耳
竟何裨爲斯民計哉噫是可爲太息也巳
punctuated:
之有方也。故適然之數不能傷如天之仁，虧允殖之治。以是知處堯湯之後，荒政尤不可已也。試以《周禮》荒政言之：散利之外，其曰薄征，以蘇其財也；曰弛役，以寛其力也。乃用之以濟荒，不可緩也。曰緩刑，以全其生也；曰蕃樂，以節其情也；曰殺盜，以除其害也。乃資之以治荒，不可廢也。若夫舍禁去譏，卽《傳》之所謂通商惠工，而非以爲縱也；眚禮殺哀，卽《易》之所謂損益盈虛，而非以爲簡也；其索鬼也，卽《詩》之所謂靡神不舉，而非以爲誣也；其多昏也，卽《易》之所謂愆期有待，而非以爲瀆也。于斯見聖人敬天之實焉，于斯見聖人勤民之政焉。《周禮》一書，誠周公致太平之書，萬世治天下者之準則也。
降及後世，履畝稅於魯，阡陌開於秦，而井田之法壞。雖代有限田、均田、口分、世業之制，亦不過剜肉補瘡之爲耳，竟何裨爲斯民計哉？噫！是可爲太息也巳！
translation_en:
…and because relief was administered by proper means. Thus the contingencies of fate could neither impair their Heaven-like benevolence nor diminish their truly flourishing government. From this we know that, for those coming after Yao and Tang, famine measures are especially indispensable. Consider the famine measures in the Rites of Zhou. Besides distributing resources, it prescribes reducing levies to restore the people’s wealth and relaxing labor service to ease the burden on their strength. These measures provide famine relief and must not be delayed. It prescribes mitigating punishments to preserve their lives, restricting music [?] to moderate their emotions, and executing robbers to eliminate threats to them. These measures support governance during famine and must not be abandoned. As for lifting prohibitions and removing inspections, these correspond to what the Commentary calls facilitating commerce and benefiting artisans; they are not intended to license unrestrained conduct. Reducing ceremonial observances and curtailing mourning correspond to what the Book of Changes calls decrease and increase, fullness and emptiness; they are not intended as mere shortcuts. Seeking out spirits corresponds to what the Book of Odes calls leaving no spirit without an offering; it is not intended as deception. Encouraging marriages corresponds to what the Book of Changes calls letting the appointed time pass while awaiting the proper occasion; it is not intended as irreverence. Here we see the substance of the sages’ reverence for Heaven; here we see their devoted governance on behalf of the people. The Rites of Zhou is truly the book through which the Duke of Zhou brought about great peace, and the standard for all who govern the world through the ages.
In later times, Lu levied taxes according to acreage, and Qin opened up the field boundaries, destroying the well-field system. Although successive ages instituted systems limiting landholdings, equalizing land allotments, allocating land by population, and providing hereditary holdings, these amounted to no more than cutting away flesh to patch a sore. What benefit, ultimately, did they bring to planning for the people’s welfare? Alas! This indeed calls for a deep sigh!

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
天生斯民寄之民牧視斯民之災歉若越
人視秦人之肥瘠而漠然不爲之所恐也
非仁人也世有升降政由俗革執揖讓之
風以議于紛爭之世而漫然必欲措之行
固也非可以議於法也新都之井田安石
之青苗其往事不旣可鑒哉愚故以爲師
其意可也達夫權可也後世爲民之計稍
爲近古者其有取於常平義倉乎常平創
於漢則耿壽昌之議也壽昌欲令邊郡築
倉穀賤則增價而糴以利農穀貴則減價
而糶以利民宣帝采之而民攸賴焉義倉
設於唐則戴胄之議也胄欲自王公以至
===
客戶有田者畝稅二升無田者分爲九等
太宗行之而時有裨焉則雖不能如周室
九年三年之積亦庶乎得儲蓄之方矣若
夫救荒之政其惟有宋諸君子乎仲淹之
興營造蔡襄之弛鹽禁皆濟一時之急至
於韓琦則蠲租稅也罷冗吏也縱流民而
punctuated:
天生斯民，寄之民牧。視斯民之災歉，若越人視秦人之肥瘠，而漠然不爲之所恐也，非仁人也。世有升降，政由俗革，執揖讓之風以議于紛爭之世，而漫然必欲措之行，固也，非可以議於法也。新都之井田、安石之青苗，其往事不旣可鑒哉？愚故以爲師其意可也，達夫權可也。後世爲民之計，稍爲近古者，其有取於常平、義倉乎？常平創於漢，則耿壽昌之議也。壽昌欲令邊郡築倉，穀賤則增價而糴，以利農；穀貴則減價而糶，以利民。宣帝采之，而民攸賴焉。義倉設於唐，則戴胄之議也。胄欲自王公以至客戶，有田者畝稅二升，無田者分爲九等。太宗行之，而時有裨焉。則雖不能如周室九年三年之積，亦庶乎得儲蓄之方矣。

若夫救荒之政，其惟有宋諸君子乎？仲淹之興營造、蔡襄之弛鹽禁，皆濟一時之急。至於韓琦，則蠲租稅也，罷冗吏也，縱流民而
translation_en:
Heaven brought forth these people and entrusted them to their shepherds. One who regards their calamities and crop failures as a person of Yue regards whether a person of Qin is well fed or emaciated, remaining indifferent and feeling no concern for them [?], is not benevolent. Ages rise and decline, and government changes with customs. To invoke the ethos of yielding and deference when discussing an age of strife, and heedlessly insist on putting it into practice, is obstinacy; such a person is unfit to discuss institutions. Do not the past examples of the well-field system of the Marquis of Xindu [Wang Mang] and the Green Sprouts program of Wang Anshi already provide warnings? I therefore humbly hold that we may emulate the intention of antiquity and understand how to adapt it to circumstances. Among later measures for the people's welfare that somewhat approached ancient practice, might there be merit in the ever-normal and charitable granaries?

The ever-normal granaries originated under the Han, on the proposal of Geng Shouchang. Shouchang wished to have granaries built in the frontier commanderies: when grain was cheap, they would purchase it at an increased price to benefit farmers; when grain was dear, they would sell it at a reduced price to benefit the people. Emperor Xuan adopted the proposal, and the people depended upon it. The charitable granaries were established under the Tang, on the proposal of Dai Zhou. Zhou proposed that, from princes and dukes down to guest households, those possessing land should pay a levy of two sheng per mu, while those without land should be divided into nine grades. Emperor Taizong implemented this, and it benefited the age. Though these measures could not provide the reserves of nine years and three years maintained by the Zhou royal house, they came close to securing a sound method of storing provisions.

As for famine relief policies, were not the gentlemen of the Song especially exemplary? Fan Zhongyan's initiation of building works and Cai Xiang's relaxation of restrictions on salt both relieved immediate emergencies. As for Han Qi, he remitted land taxes, dismissed superfluous officials, and allowed displaced people to move freely and…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
不禁也募入粟而行賞也當時之民所由
以全活者甚衆朱子則放田租也勸出粟
也招誘商人也戒飭官吏也一郡之民咸
安堵不至遷徙是雖不至如周官弛役眚
禮之法亦庶乎得濟時之策矣雖然朱子
亦嘗言之曰自古救荒有二事其一感召
和氣次則備儲之計耳又曰救荒之政固
當蠲除賑貸尤在撫養存恤譬之病者湯
劑砭炙不可緩也將護節宣尤不可失宜
由此觀之則濟之於已然者拯捄之方也
消之於未然者感通之道也方今
===
聖明御極純敬格
天太和熏烝雨暘時若敦治道於湯穆囿天下
於咸熙固有以追成周之盛而媲美之矣
邇者河北蝗旱交作江南水潦頻仍至厪
九重軫念下賑貸寬恤之令無乃奉行
德意者有未至歟或未盡舉成周之法而施之
歟愚則又有說焉是故其務有五曰開民
punctuated:
不禁也，募入粟而行賞也。當時之民所由以全活者甚衆。朱子則放田租也，勸出粟也，招誘商人也，戒飭官吏也。一郡之民咸安堵，不至遷徙。是雖不至如周官弛役眚禮之法，亦庶乎得濟時之策矣。雖然，朱子亦嘗言之曰：「自古救荒有二事，其一感召和氣，次則備儲之計耳。」又曰：「救荒之政，固當蠲除賑貸，尤在撫養存恤。譬之病者，湯劑砭炙不可緩也，將護節宣尤不可失宜。」由此觀之，則濟之於已然者，拯捄之方也；消之於未然者，感通之道也。
方今聖明御極，純敬格天，太和熏烝，雨暘時若。敦治道於湯穆，囿天下於咸熙，固有以追成周之盛而媲美之矣。邇者河北蝗旱交作，江南水潦頻仍，至厪九重軫念，下賑貸寬恤之令。無乃奉行德意者有未至歟？或未盡舉成周之法而施之歟？愚則又有說焉。是故其務有五：曰開民
translation_en:
…without prohibiting their movement, and offering rewards to recruit contributors of grain. Very many people at the time survived through these measures. Master Zhu, for his part, remitted land taxes, encouraged grain contributions, attracted merchants, and admonished officials. The people throughout the prefecture remained secure in their homes and did not have to migrate. Although these measures did not attain the standard of the methods in the Offices of Zhou for relaxing labor services and reducing ceremonial observances, they came close to providing an effective response to the needs of the time. Nevertheless, Master Zhu also once said: “Since antiquity, famine relief has involved two things: first, calling forth harmonious vital forces; next, making plans to store provisions.” He also said: “Famine relief certainly requires tax remissions, relief distributions, and loans, but above all it depends on nurturing and caring for the people. It is like treating a sick person: medicinal decoctions, stone needling, and moxibustion must not be delayed, but attentive nursing and the proper regulation of bodily functions must especially be suited to the circumstances.” Viewed in this light, providing relief after disaster has occurred is a method of rescue; dispelling it before it occurs is the way of eliciting a response through sympathetic resonance.
Now our sage and enlightened sovereign occupies the throne. His pure reverence reaches Heaven; supreme harmony pervades all, and rain and sunshine arrive in season. He cultivates the way of governance in Tang and Mu [?], bringing all under Heaven into universal prosperity. There is indeed good reason to say that he approaches and rivals the flourishing age of Zhou. Recently, however, locusts and drought have struck Hebei together, while floods have repeatedly afflicted Jiangnan. These have troubled His Majesty with concern and prompted him to issue orders for relief distributions, loans, and compassionate concessions. Could those charged with carrying out his benevolent intentions have fallen short? Or have the methods of Zhou not yet been fully adopted and applied? I, in my humble opinion, have a further argument to offer. Accordingly, there are five essential tasks. The first is to “open up the people” [?]…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
麗也曰重民命也曰恤民力也曰剔民蠹
也曰急民患也夫成周式重農事夫家之
罰閑民則轉移執事皆務本業而今之好
閒者多矣故曰民罷之當閑也周禮五聽
三宥惟恐民之罹于刑而今罰必罷于事
令之好肉鼓吹而草菅者有矣故曰民命
之當重也古者使民以時故特紲舉嬴君
子非之今之州縣之民疲于奔命者衆矣
故曰民力之當恤也古之君子律身以廉
===
如清獻之琴鶴自隨至今稱之今世則有
歐陽子所謂居官致富爲豪傑者比比然
也故曰民蠹之當剔也昔秦饑晉閉之糴
春秋譏之今之司牧秦越其心而民瘼罔
念矣故曰民患之當急也夫民罷閑則衣
食充而饑寒之累鮮矣民命重則公道行
而寃抑之苦伸矣民力恤則家室安而不
病于流離之厄民蠹剔則貪墨懲而不困
于剝削之苛民患急則上下協而成一體
punctuated:
麗也，曰重民命也，曰恤民力也，曰剔民蠹也，曰急民患也。夫成周式重農事，夫家之罰，閑民則轉移執事，皆務本業，而今之好閒者多矣。故曰民罷之當閑也。《周禮》五聽三宥，惟恐民之罹于刑，而今罰必罷于事，令之好肉鼓吹而草菅者有矣。故曰民命之當重也。古者使民以時，故特紲舉嬴，君子非之。今之州縣之民，疲于奔命者衆矣。故曰民力之當恤也。古之君子律身以廉，如清獻之琴鶴自隨，至今稱之。今世則有歐陽子所謂居官致富爲豪傑者，比比然也。故曰民蠹之當剔也。昔秦饑，晉閉之糴，《春秋》譏之。今之司牧，秦越其心，而民瘼罔念矣。故曰民患之當急也。
夫民罷閑，則衣食充而饑寒之累鮮矣；民命重，則公道行而寃抑之苦伸矣；民力恤，則家室安而不病于流離之厄；民蠹剔，則貪墨懲而不困于剝削之苛；民患急，則上下協而成一體
translation_en:
…[the conclusion of the first measure is garbled: 麗也]. The others are to value the people's lives, to spare the people's strength, to remove those who prey upon the people, and to attend urgently to the people's hardships. The Zhou held agricultural work in particular esteem: penalties were imposed upon households, and people without regular occupations were assigned to different kinds of work, so that all attended to their fundamental livelihoods. Today, however, many prefer idleness. Thus I say that the people's indolence must be restrained [?]. The Rites of Zhou prescribed five methods of examining testimony and three grounds for pardon, out of profound concern lest the people suffer punishment. Today, however, punishments and official business are mishandled [?], and there are those who delight in meat and music while treating human lives like worthless grass [?]. Thus I say that the people's lives must be valued. In antiquity, the people's labor was employed only at the proper seasons; hence gentlemen condemned “特紲舉嬴” [an obscure, apparently garbled phrase]. Today, many people in the prefectures and counties are exhausted by rushing to obey official commands. Thus I say that the people's strength must be spared. The gentlemen of antiquity disciplined themselves through incorruptibility. Qingxian, for example, traveled with his zither and crane, and is praised to this day. In our own age, however, those whom Master Ouyang described as regarding enrichment through office as the mark of a great man are everywhere. Thus I say that those who prey upon the people must be removed. In the past, when Qin suffered famine, Jin barred its purchase of grain, and the Spring and Autumn Annals condemned this. Today, those charged with governing the people are as indifferent to them as Qin and Yue were to one another, giving no thought to the people's afflictions. Thus I say that the people's hardships must be treated as urgent.
When the people's indolence is restrained [?], clothing and food will be plentiful, and the burdens of hunger and cold will be few. When their lives are valued, justice will prevail, and the suffering caused by wrongful treatment and oppression will be redressed. When their strength is spared, their households will be secure, and they will not suffer the misery of displacement. When those who prey upon them are removed, corrupt officials will be punished, and the people will not be distressed by cruel exploitation. When their hardships are treated as urgent, those above and below will act in harmony and become one body…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之義至於我
國家設預備倉亦今之常平義倉也若果責
實而行儲積有方贖鍰俱令入粟紅腐以
時易新有司計數而攷其績監司核籍以
稽其弊一遇荒歉本所謂十二政者參諸
歷代之法酌而行之是亦求三年之艾於
自今之畜也不然旱甚而爲之圖猶之夸
父臨渴而索勺水漁父臨淵而後羨魚也
烏能有濟哉
===
吳世登
考試官教諭陳　批
指摘貴州時事如在目中
而綜理區畫鑿鑿有見當事者誠不以文字目之黔中
赤子會見衽席之安矣
考試官教諭陳　批
劃四府司四邊衛隸之貴
省無謂其不可者第末之行爾是篇及此俊傑之士也
第五問
嘗聞之智者審事幾以濟時仁人弘度量
以體國故圖難於其易爲大於其細哲人
punctuated:
之義。至於我國家設預備倉，亦今之常平義倉也。若果責實而行，儲積有方，贖鍰俱令入粟，紅腐以時易新，有司計數而攷其績，監司核籍以稽其弊，一遇荒歉，本所謂十二政者，參諸歷代之法，酌而行之，是亦求三年之艾於自今之畜也。不然，旱甚而爲之圖，猶之夸父臨渴而索勺水，漁父臨淵而後羨魚也，烏能有濟哉？

吳世登

考試官教諭陳批：指摘貴州時事，如在目中，而綜理區畫，鑿鑿有見。當事者誠不以文字目之，黔中赤子會見衽席之安矣。

考試官教諭陳批：劃四府司、四邊衛隸之貴省，無謂其不可者，第末之行爾。是篇及此，俊傑之士也。

第五問

嘗聞之，智者審事幾以濟時，仁人弘度量以體國。故圖難於其易，爲大於其細，哲人
translation_en:
…the principle of forming a single body. As for the reserve granaries established by our dynasty, these too are the ever-normal and charitable granaries of the present day. If their administration truly demanded concrete results, if grain were stored by proper methods, if all redemption fines were paid in grain, and if reddened and decaying grain were replaced with fresh grain in due season; if the responsible officials calculated the quantities to assess their achievements, and the surveillance officials checked the registers to investigate abuses—then, whenever a poor harvest occurred, the aforementioned twelve measures could serve as the basis, considered alongside the methods of successive dynasties and implemented as circumstances required. This too would be like beginning now to store mugwort in order to obtain a supply aged for three years. Otherwise, to devise measures only when drought has become severe would be like Kuafu seeking a ladleful of water only when thirst overtook him, or a fisherman reaching the deep pool before longing for fish. How could this bring any relief?

Wu Shideng

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor:
His identification of current problems in Guizhou makes them seem present before our eyes, while his comprehensive organization and planning show clear and solid insight. If those responsible truly regard this as more than a literary composition, the beloved people of Qian will surely enjoy the security and ease of resting upon their bedding.

Comment by Examiner Chen, Instructor:
To place the four prefectural offices [?] and four frontier guards under the jurisdiction of Guizhou Province—no one says this is impracticable; it has simply not yet been carried out [?]. That this essay addresses this matter shows its author to be a man of outstanding ability.

Fifth Question

I have heard that the wise scrutinize the first signs of developments in order to meet the needs of their times, while the humane broaden their capacity for tolerance in order to serve the interests of the state. Thus, to plan for difficulties while they are still easy, and to undertake great things while they are still small—this is the wise person's…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
之見也裒多益寡損有餘補不足大公之
猷也貴州之勢則可謂大壞極弊矣董子
曰琴瑟不調甚者必解而更張之乃可鼓
也爲貴計者而不更張雖使孟氏畫策管
仲執籌未有能救者也夫體國以濟時者
視天下猶一身而其視天下之人猶一家
也今有人焉體貌豐碩腹心無恙也忽手
足痿痺慘然見乎其色有得秦越人之方
者必褁糧以求之千金之家或孽子不能
===
供朝夕從執父券而責之於推分也可乎夫
謂手足之無預於身謂孽子之無關於家
非智也視其痿痺而不治視其匱乏而不
恤非仁也今夫貴州上下山磵無曠衍之
土則賦稅無出也椎髻跣足無編户之氓
則生齒不繁也自
國初徙諸省居民塡實于貴列于戍籍非不
知民之懷土重遷也不如是不足以供一
省之備禦邇來軍士逃亡者十常八九冊
punctuated: 之見也。裒多益寡，損有餘補不足，大公之猷也。貴州之勢，則可謂大壞極弊矣。董子曰：「琴瑟不調，甚者必解而更張之，乃可鼓也。」爲貴計者而不更張，雖使孟氏畫策，管仲執籌，未有能救者也。夫體國以濟時者，視天下猶一身，而其視天下之人猶一家也。今有人焉，體貌豐碩，腹心無恙也，忽手足痿痺，慘然見乎其色，有得秦越人之方者，必褁糧以求之。千金之家，或孽子不能供朝夕，從執父券而責之於推分也，可乎？夫謂手足之無預於身，謂孽子之無關於家，非智也；視其痿痺而不治，視其匱乏而不恤，非仁也。今夫貴州，上下山磵，無曠衍之土，則賦稅無出也；椎髻跣足，無編户之氓，則生齒不繁也。自國初徙諸省居民塡實于貴，列于戍籍，非不知民之懷土重遷也，不如是不足以供一省之備禦。邇來軍士逃亡者十常八九，冊
translation_en:
…such is the insight of the wise. To take from those who have much and augment those who have little, reducing surpluses to make up deficiencies, is the principle of utmost impartiality. Guizhou’s condition may indeed be described as one of utter ruin and extreme deterioration. Master Dong said: “When a zither is badly out of tune, its strings must be loosened and restrung before it can be played.” If those planning for Guizhou do not likewise make fundamental changes, even with Mencius devising policies and Guan Zhong handling calculations, no one could save it.

Those who serve the state and meet the needs of the times regard all under Heaven as one body, and its people as one family. Suppose someone is robust in appearance, with his internal organs free of illness, but suddenly his hands and feet become weak and numb. Distress appears on his face; if anyone possesses a remedy handed down by Qin Yueren, he will certainly pack provisions and go in search of it. In a wealthy household, suppose a son born of a concubine cannot provide for his daily meals: would it be acceptable to hold his father’s deed and insist that he rely on his allotted share [?]? To say that hands and feet have nothing to do with the body, or that a concubine’s son has nothing to do with the family, is not wisdom. To see their weakness and numbness without treating them, or their want without relieving it, is not benevolence.

Now Guizhou consists of mountains and ravines rising and falling, with no broad, level land; thus there is no source of tax revenue. Its people wear their hair in mallet-shaped knots and go barefoot, and there are no people enrolled in household registers; thus its registered population is not numerous. From the founding of the dynasty, inhabitants of other provinces were relocated to populate Guizhou and entered in the garrison registers. This was not because the authorities failed to understand that people cherish their native soil and are reluctant to move. Without such measures, however, the defensive needs of the province could not have been met. Recently, eight or nine soldiers out of every ten have commonly deserted. As for the registers…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
籍清勾者十無一二司牧之官乃以爲委
瑣之務漫不爲塡補也自
國初派川湖稅糧轉給于貴著爲令甲非不
知彼之不可與此也不如是不足以供諸
衛之饋餉邇來湖南之逋負者十之三四
川西之逋負者十之七八抑方之士猶以
爲他省之賦□漫不爲徵輸也往年鎭筸之
變議調兵戍□銅仁省平頭衛士則更番入
直游卒則□名募寄□□饟無所措至借官
===
軍之額派給客兵之□增即邊境晏然一
歲之入已難支一歲之用董董不足更費
也有如饑饉相仍寇盜有警舟車所不通
販糴所不至司計者則謂之何近日韓甸
之逆集羣蠻寇旅秉窺鎭遠我兵興則鳥
驚鼠竄我兵散則豕突獸馳夫縣雖屬貴
而容山川之轄也衛屯湖之隸也即貴省
全盛猶當用三省之力除三省之患章章
明甚也矧貴公私兩竭軍民俱困芻粟所
punctuated: 籍清勾者十無一二。司牧之官乃以爲委瑣之務，漫不爲塡補也。自國初派川湖稅糧轉給于貴，著爲令甲，非不知彼之不可與此也，不如是不足以供諸衛之饋餉。邇來湖南之逋負者十之三四，川西之逋負者十之七八，抑方之士猶以爲他省之賦□，漫不爲徵輸也。往年鎭筸之變，議調兵戍□銅仁，省平頭衛士則更番入直，游卒則□名募寄□□，饟無所措，至借官軍之額，派給客兵之□增。即邊境晏然，一歲之入已難支一歲之用，董董不足更費也。有如饑饉相仍，寇盜有警，舟車所不通，販糴所不至，司計者則謂之何？近日韓甸之逆，集羣蠻寇旅秉，窺鎭遠。我兵興則鳥驚鼠竄，我兵散則豕突獸馳。夫縣雖屬貴，而容山川之轄也，衛屯湖之隸也。即貴省全盛，猶當用三省之力，除三省之患，章章明甚也。矧貴公私兩竭，軍民俱困，芻粟所
translation_en:
…of those on the registers, not even one or two in ten are recovered through roster checks and requisitions. Yet the officials charged with governing regard this as a trifling matter and carelessly neglect to fill the vacancies. Since the dynasty’s founding, tax grain from Sichuan and Huguang has been assigned for transfer to Guizhou, a provision established by statute. It was not that the authorities failed to understand that those provinces could ill afford to give to this one; without this arrangement, the various guards could not be provisioned. Recently, arrears in southern Huguang have reached three or four tenths, and those in western Sichuan seven or eight tenths. Yet the regional officials [?] still regard these as another province’s taxes [illegible] and carelessly neglect their collection and shipment.

During the disturbances at Zheng an 鎭筸 in earlier years, it was proposed to transfer troops to garrison [illegible] Tongren. The passage concerning the guard soldiers of Pingtou is doubtful [?], but they were to take turns entering upon duty; unattached soldiers were to be recruited and registered [?; several characters illegible]. No means could be found to provide their rations, and it even became necessary to draw upon the regular troops’ allotments to supply the additional requirements [?] of the troops brought in from elsewhere. Even when the frontier is peaceful, one year’s receipts already scarcely cover one year’s expenditure; there is insufficient provision for further expenses [?]. If famine should recur and bandit incursions raise the alarm, in places inaccessible to boats and carts and beyond the reach of grain merchants and purchases, what would those responsible for finances have to say?

Recently, the rebel Han Dian gathered the various Man peoples, attacked Lübing [?], and cast his eye upon Zhenyuan. When our troops advance, they scatter like startled birds and fleeing rats; when our troops disperse, they charge like boars and race like wild beasts. Although the county belongs to Guizhou, Rongshan [?] falls under Sichuan’s jurisdiction, while the guard’s agricultural colonies are subordinate to Huguang. Even were Guizhou at the height of its strength, the resources of all three provinces ought still to be used to eliminate a danger shared by all three. This is abundantly clear. How much more so when Guizhou’s public and private resources are both exhausted, its soldiers and civilians alike distressed, and fodder and grain …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
不產飛輓所不及籌邊者則謂之何或者
曰四邊衛可割也蓋平溪清浪偏橋鎮遠
其屯種錯雜於民間而鎮遠與府同一處
也雖名兼制而莫能制其命往苗夷竊發
四衛每以異省爲辭文移往復動經數月
竟致攻陷城堡屠戮人民必勞
朝廷遣兵將而後定也又況鄉舉生徒在貴
則解額附名在湖則士籍削迹故湖之視
四衛猶越人視秦人之肥瘠而四衛之視
===
貴猶子弟衛父兄手足捍頭目知府周瑛
嘗奏
請矣其議有不可行乎或者曰四府司可割也
蓋播州鎮雄烏蒙烏撒其疆域深懸於貴
境而烏撒與衛又同一城也雖名兼制而
莫能握其樞纂年例積逋諸司每以異省
藉口遣官催徵動踰數月非空文抵飾則
薄與塞責必請督府勤守臣而後可也又
況追攝罪人在川則歲淹而月延在貴則
punctuated:
不產，飛輓所不及，籌邊者則謂之何？或者曰：「四邊衛可割也。」蓋平溪、清浪、偏橋、鎮遠，其屯種錯雜於民間，而鎮遠與府同一處也。雖名兼制，而莫能制其命。往苗夷竊發，四衛每以異省爲辭，文移往復，動經數月，竟致攻陷城堡，屠戮人民，必勞朝廷遣兵將而後定也。又況鄉舉生徒，在貴則解額附名，在湖則士籍削迹。故湖之視四衛，猶越人視秦人之肥瘠；而四衛之視貴，猶子弟衛父兄、手足捍頭目。知府周瑛嘗奏請矣，其議有不可行乎？

或者曰：「四府司可割也。」蓋播州、鎮雄、烏蒙、烏撒，其疆域深懸於貴境，而烏撒與衛又同一城也。雖名兼制，而莫能握其樞。纂年例積逋，諸司每以異省藉口，遣官催徵，動踰數月，非空文抵飾，則薄與塞責，必請督府勤守臣而後可也。又況追攝罪人，在川則歲淹而月延，在貴則
translation_en:
…where fodder and grain are not produced and expedited transport cannot reach—what do those who plan frontier defense say to this? Some say: “The four frontier Guards could be transferred.” These are Pingxi, Qinglang, Pianqiao, and Zhenyuan. Their military farming lands are interspersed among civilian settlements, and the Zhenyuan Guard occupies the same site as the prefectural seat. Although nominally subject to concurrent jurisdiction, no one can effectively command them. In the past, when the Miao rose in rebellion, the four Guards repeatedly pleaded that they belonged to another province. Official correspondence went back and forth, often taking several months, until forts were captured and the people slaughtered. Only after the court was troubled to dispatch troops and commanders could order be restored. Moreover, students seeking to take the Provincial Examination have their names included under Guizhou’s quota, while in Huguang their names are struck from the registers of scholars. Thus Huguang regards the four Guards as a person of Yue regards a person of Qin’s stoutness or thinness—with indifference. The four Guards, however, regard Guizhou as sons and younger brothers defend their fathers and elder brothers, or hands and feet protect the head and eyes. Prefect Zhou Ying once memorialized requesting this. Is there anything impracticable in his proposal?

Some say: “The four prefectures and offices could be transferred.” These are Bozhou, Zhenxiong, Wumeng, and Wusa. Their territories lie deep within Guizhou, and Wusa and the Guard there occupy the same city. Although nominally subject to concurrent jurisdiction, no one can effectively control their workings. Annual obligations accumulate in arrears [?], and these offices repeatedly use their affiliation with another province as an excuse. When officials are dispatched to press for payment, several months often pass. They either offer empty documents to evade and conceal matters or pay a paltry amount to discharge their responsibility. Only by petitioning the supreme commander to press the local officials into action can anything be accomplished. Moreover, when pursuing and arresting offenders, handling the matter through Sichuan means delays stretching through months and years; through Guizhou, however, …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
朝發而夕至故川之視四司猶鞭之長不
及馬腹而四司之視貴則猶同室有鬬不
必借援於千里兩省憲臣嘗奏
請矣其議有不可行乎甞謂是衛司者自川湖
觀之爲彈丸黑子失之不爲損自貴州觀
之爲門庭之內卧榻之側待之爲有益不
然徒執彼疆我里之說版圖定分之說而
不爲之更張則貴以困憊之餘而當多事
之際是亦杯水救燎原之焰剜肉醫眼前
===
之瘡必至往來之襟喉以塞西南之門户
以阻滇中之貢賦不通有識者且將食不
下咽而烏能一日安其職也
punctuated: 朝發而夕至。故川之視四司，猶鞭之長不及馬腹；而四司之視貴，則猶同室有鬬，不必借援於千里。兩省憲臣嘗奏請矣，其議有不可行乎？甞謂是衛司者，自川湖觀之，爲彈丸黑子，失之不爲損；自貴州觀之，爲門庭之內、卧榻之側，待之爲有益。不然，徒執彼疆我里之說、版圖定分之說，而不爲之更張，則貴以困憊之餘，而當多事之際，是亦杯水救燎原之焰，剜肉醫眼前之瘡，必至往來之襟喉以塞，西南之門户以阻，滇中之貢賦不通。有識者且將食不下咽，而烏能一日安其職也？
translation_en:
…one could set out in the morning and arrive by evening. Thus, Sichuan’s relationship to the four native offices is like a whip that, though long, cannot reach the horse’s belly. The four offices’ relationship to Guizhou, however, is like a quarrel within the same household: there is no need to seek assistance a thousand li away. The censorial officials of the two provinces have already memorialized the throne to request this. Is there anything impracticable about their proposal?

I have long maintained that these guards and native offices, viewed from Sichuan and Huguang, are mere pellets or tiny black spots: losing them would cause no harm. Viewed from Guizhou, however, they lie within its own courtyard and beside its bed; relying on them would be beneficial. Otherwise, if we merely cling to arguments about ‘their territory and our lands’ and the fixed apportionment of administrative boundaries, without making changes, then Guizhou, already exhausted, must confront a time of many troubles. This would be like trying to extinguish a prairie fire with a cup of water, or cutting away flesh to treat an immediate sore. It would inevitably leave the vital passage for travel blocked [?], obstruct the gateway to the southwest, and prevent tribute and tax revenues from Yunnan from passing through. Those who understand the situation would be unable to swallow their food. How could they remain at ease in their duties for even a single day?

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
貴州鄉試錄後序
維辛酉貴州貢士典成至是
舉行者九夫貴昔嘗附滇省
薦書今則詩設科矣貴昔預
選者二十五人今則特增解
額爲三十人矣是唐虞野無
遺賢成周不忘遠之心也貴
===
雖遐荒視諸省獨遠其感被
湛恩而願效忠視諸省當獨深
也方今
龍飛四十禩所取多士固生長泰
平之世涵濡
聖化有得者茲於其始進敬申一
言答鹿鳴之貺嘗讀孔氏春
punctuated:
貴州鄉試錄後序

維辛酉，貴州貢士典成，至是舉行者九。夫貴昔嘗附滇省薦書，今則詩設科矣。貴昔預選者二十五人，今則特增解額爲三十人矣。是唐虞野無遺賢、成周不忘遠之心也。貴雖遐荒，視諸省獨遠，其感被湛恩而願效忠，視諸省當獨深也。方今龍飛四十禩，所取多士固生長泰平之世，涵濡聖化有得者。茲於其始進，敬申一言，答鹿鳴之貺。嘗讀孔氏春
translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Guizhou Provincial Examination

In the xinyou year [1561], the ceremony for selecting tribute scholars in Guizhou was completed; this was its ninth holding. Formerly, Guizhou’s candidates were included in Yunnan Province’s list of recommended men; now an examination has been established for Guizhou itself [the character 詩 is doubtful]. Formerly, twenty-five men from Guizhou were selected; now its provincial quota has been specially increased to thirty. This embodies the spirit of the ages of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, when no worthy man in the countryside was overlooked, and of the Zhou dynasty, which did not forget distant regions. Although Guizhou is a remote frontier land, farther away than any other province, its gratitude for the profound imperial favor it has received, and its desire to render loyal service, should accordingly be deeper than those of any other province.

Now, in the fortieth year since His Majesty ascended the throne, the many scholars selected have indeed grown up in an age of peace and benefited from immersion in the sage sovereign’s transforming influence. As they take their first steps toward official service, I respectfully offer a few words in return for the favor of the Deer-Crying Banquet. I once read Confucius’s Spring …

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
秋知人才在霄壤間氣運有
時推移疆域非所限隔夫荊
楚吳越春秋嘗比諸夷有能
自通上國惓惓接引所謂來
則嘉其慕義而接之以禮也
夫湖湘三吳兩浙非故荊楚
吳越之區乎今文獻冠裳甲
===
於海內山川風物視往時何
如也貴陽自昔不通賓貢太
史公傳諸西南夷入
國朝始列藩服置衛興學自丁
酉開科以來文學彬彬與中
土埒矣當
聖人久道化成之候雖卉服椎髻
punctuated: 秋，知人才在霄壤間，氣運有時推移，疆域非所限隔。夫荊楚吳越，春秋嘗比諸夷，有能自通上國，惓惓接引，所謂來則嘉其慕義而接之以禮也。夫湖湘、三吳、兩浙，非故荊楚吳越之區乎？今文獻冠裳甲於海內，山川風物視往時何如也？貴陽自昔不通賓貢，太史公傳諸西南夷。入國朝，始列藩服，置衛興學。自丁酉開科以來，文學彬彬，與中土埒矣。當聖人久道化成之候，雖卉服椎髻
translation_en:
…Autumn Annals, I learned that, between heaven and earth, the currents of fortune that produce talented people shift over time; territorial boundaries do not confine them. Jing, Chu, Wu, and Yue were once classed with the barbarians in the Spring and Autumn Annals. Yet when any could establish relations with the central states, they were solicitously welcomed and guided forward. This is what is meant by saying that, when they came, their admiration for righteousness was commended and they were received with ritual courtesy. Are Huxiang, the Three Wu, and the Two Zhe not the former territories of Jing, Chu, Wu, and Yue? Today their writings, learned worthies, and men in official dress rank foremost within the seas. How do their mountains, rivers, local customs, and products compare with those of former times?

Guiyang had not formerly participated in the presentation of tribute candidates; the Grand Historian treated it among the Southwestern Barbarians. Only under our dynasty was it incorporated into the realm’s outlying territories, with guards established and schools promoted. Since the examinations were inaugurated in the dingyou year, literary learning has flourished, matching that of the central regions. At this time, when the sage ruler’s long adherence to the Way has brought his transforming influence to fruition, even those wearing garments of plant fiber and mallet-shaped topknots…

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
循喁喁嚮風矧爾章縫之士
沐文明之化誦仁義之說而
不思自效于
明時以樹尺寸是殊類之不逮也
且攷之載記丹砂產自萬山
其上品光明中品白馬牙下
品紫金是三品在深崖幽谷
===
舟車所不通世方以爲有益
於用採購者至竆其力之所
能而未必可得疇能以遠方
之物鄙之也使或不得其眞
而取瓦礫與沙石無適于用
矣士之品亦有三上焉者立
德中焉者立功下焉者立言
punctuated:
循喁喁嚮風，矧爾章縫之士，沐文明之化，誦仁義之說，而不思自效于明時，以樹尺寸，是殊類之不逮也。
且攷之載記，丹砂產自萬山，其上品光明，中品白馬牙，下品紫金。是三品在深崖幽谷，舟車所不通。世方以爲有益於用，採購者至竆其力之所能，而未必可得，疇能以遠方之物鄙之也？使或不得其眞，而取瓦礫與沙石，無適于用矣。士之品亦有三：上焉者立德，中焉者立功，下焉者立言。
translation_en:
…eagerly turn toward your civilizing influence [?]. How much more should you scholars wearing the Confucian cap, who have bathed in the transforming influence of cultivated enlightenment and recite teachings of benevolence and righteousness! If you do not think of offering your service in this enlightened age and establishing even a modest achievement, you fall short of those peoples of different customs.
Moreover, consulting the written records, cinnabar is produced in Wanshan. Its highest grade is called “Brilliant,” its middle grade “White Horse’s Teeth,” and its lowest grade “Purple Gold.” These three grades lie among deep cliffs and secluded valleys, beyond the reach of boats and carts. People regard them as useful, and those who gather and purchase them exhaust all their powers, yet may still fail to obtain them. Who could disdain them as mere products of a distant region? If, however, one fails to obtain the genuine substance and takes instead broken tiles, gravel, sand, and stones, these will serve no useful purpose. Scholars likewise have three grades: the highest establish virtue, the middle establish achievements, and the lowest establish enduring words.

title: 嘉靖四十年貴州鄉試錄
text:
匪是則今之所取蠟言爾人
將沙礫視之矣爾諸生顧寧
以是自待乎典文者日兢兢
焉而不容釋也諸生其勗之
哉
河南衛輝府獲嘉縣儒學教
諭陳安謹序
punctuated:
匪是，則今之所取，蠟言爾，人將沙礫視之矣。爾諸生顧寧以是自待乎？典文者日兢兢焉，而不容釋也。諸生其勗之哉！
河南衛輝府獲嘉縣儒學教諭陳安謹序。
translation_en:
…Without these, what is selected today amounts merely to “waxen words” [?], which people will regard as sand and gravel. Would you students really be content to regard yourselves in this way? Those charged with judging literary compositions remain vigilant every day and cannot permit themselves to relax. You students, strive hard!
Preface respectfully composed by Chen An, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huojia County, Weihui Prefecture, Henan.
